title: An Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 epitope peptide vaccine promotes dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity in a murine HPV16 tumor model, with greater tumor control upon PD-1 blockade.
abstract: Background Therapeutic vaccines targeting human papillomavirus (HPV) E6/E7 oncoproteins represent a promising strategy for cervical cancer immunotherapy, yet most candidates remain constrained by insufficient antigen presentation efficiency and suboptimal T-cell responses. The Ii-Key strategy, which links the invariant chain (Ii) core motif to epitope peptides to facilitate MHC class II loading, may overcome this limitation by amplifying CD4 + T helper responses. Methods HPV16/18 E7 epitopes restricted by murine H-2 class I/II molecules were predicted using immunoinformatics tools. Ii-Key-modified MHC class II peptides (LRMK-PEG2-epitope) and unmodified MHC class I peptides were synthesized and evaluated in vitro using bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC) stimulation assays with flow cytometry, ELISA, and western blotting. In vivo immunogenicity was assessed in C57BL/6 mice through immune phenotyping of lymphoid organs and plasma cytokine profiling. Anti-tumor activity was tested in an early-intervention subcutaneous TC-1 tumor model (HPV16 E6/E7-positive) with histopathological and flow cytometric analyses of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. Combination treatment with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody was also examined. Results The peptide pool promoted BMDC maturation, as evidenced by increased frequencies of CD80 + CD86 + and I-A/I-E + BMDCs, NF-κB pathway activation, and increased proinflammatory cytokine secretion; these readouts indicate DC activation. In C57BL/6 mice, peptide immunization induced DC activation in draining lymph nodes, enhanced CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell activation (CD8 + increase significant only in non-tumor-bearing mice), reduced Treg proportions in tumor-bearing mice (with a non-significant decline in non-tumor-bearing mice), elicited direct ex vivo splenocyte cytotoxicity against TC-1 cells, and altered memory-phenotype T-cell frequencies, increasing TCM frequency in non-tumor-bearing mice and TEM frequency in tumor-bearing mice. In the TC-1 model, peptide treatment suppressed tumor growth and qualitatively reduced tumor Ki67 staining, accompanied by non-significant trends toward increased intratumoral CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell frequencies. Combination with anti-PD-1 produced greater tumor control than either monotherapy. Safety assessments by histopathology and serum biochemistry indicated acceptable tolerability under the conditions and observation period tested. Conclusions The Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 peptide formulation promoted dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity, achieving anti-tumor activity in an early-intervention TC-1 model with acceptable tolerability. The combination with PD-1 blockade produced greater tumor control than either monotherapy; this comparison does not establish additivity or synergy. These preclinical findings support further evaluation of the formulation incorporating direct antigen-presentation assays and matched unmodified MHC-II peptide controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of an Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 epitope peptide vaccine to promote dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity in a murine HPV16 tumor model. The research aimed to address the limitations of current therapeutic vaccines, which often suffer from poor antigen presentation and suboptimal T-cell responses. The study design involved in vitro and in vivo assessments using immunoinformatics tools, BMDC stimulation assays, and a TC-1 tumor model. The main results showed that the vaccine formulation enhanced dendritic cell maturation and activated T-cell responses, leading to tumor suppression. The combination of the vaccine with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody demonstrated greater tumor control than either treatment alone. The findings suggest that this approach could improve therapeutic vaccines against HPV-associated cancers, but the study lacks long-term safety data and human trial information, limiting the strength of the evidence.

title_zh: 含Ii-Key的HPV16/18 E7表位肽疫苗促进树突状细胞激活和T细胞免疫,在小鼠HPV16肿瘤模型中表现出更强的肿瘤控制效果,联合PD-1阻断剂效果更佳。
source_body_en: Background Therapeutic vaccines targeting human papillomavirus (HPV) E6/E7 oncoproteins represent a promising strategy for cervical cancer immunotherapy, yet most candidates remain constrained by insufficient antigen presentation efficiency and suboptimal T-cell responses. The Ii-Key strategy, which links the invariant chain (Ii) core motif to epitope peptides to facilitate MHC class II loading, may overcome this limitation by amplifying CD4 + T helper responses. Methods HPV16/18 E7 epitopes restricted by murine H-2 class I/II molecules were predicted using immunoinformatics tools. Ii-Key-modified MHC class II peptides (LRMK-PEG2-epitope) and unmodified MHC class I peptides were synthesized and evaluated in vitro using bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC) stimulation assays with flow cytometry, ELISA, and western blotting. In vivo immunogenicity was assessed in C57BL/6 mice through immune phenotyping of lymphoid organs and plasma cytokine profiling. Anti-tumor activity was tested in an early-intervention subcutaneous TC-1 tumor model (HPV16 E6/E7-positive) with histopathological and flow cytometric analyses of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. Combination treatment with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody was also examined. Results The peptide pool promoted BMDC maturation, as evidenced by increased frequencies of CD80 + CD86 + and I-A/I-E + BMDCs, NF-κB pathway activation, and increased proinflammatory cytokine secretion; these readouts indicate DC activation. In C57BL/6 mice, peptide immunization induced DC activation in draining lymph nodes, enhanced CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell activation (CD8 + increase significant only in non-tumor-bearing mice), reduced Treg proportions in tumor-bearing mice (with a non-significant decline in non-tumor-bearing mice), elicited direct ex vivo splenocyte cytotoxicity against TC-1 cells, and altered memory-phenotype T-cell frequencies, increasing TCM frequency in non-tumor-bearing mice and TEM frequency in tumor-bearing mice. In the TC-1 model, peptide treatment suppressed tumor growth and qualitatively reduced tumor Ki67 staining, accompanied by non-significant trends toward increased intratumoral CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell frequencies. Combination with anti-PD-1 produced greater tumor control than either monotherapy. Safety assessments by histopathology and serum biochemistry indicated acceptable tolerability under the conditions and observation period tested. Conclusions The Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 peptide formulation promoted dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity, achieving anti-tumor activity in an early-intervention TC-1 model with acceptable tolerability. The combination with PD-1 blockade produced greater tumor control than either monotherapy; this comparison does not establish additivity or synergy. These preclinical findings support further evaluation of the formulation incorporating direct antigen-presentation assays and matched unmodified MHC-II peptide controls.
abstract_zh: 背景 针对HPV E6/E7癌蛋白的治疗性疫苗在宫颈癌免疫治疗中具有广阔前景,但大多数候选药物仍受限于抗原呈递效率不足和T细胞反应不理想。Ii-Key策略通过将不变链(Ii)核心模体与表位肽连接,以促进MHC II类分子的装载,可能通过增强CD4+ T辅助细胞反应来克服这一限制。方法 使用免疫信息学工具预测了HPV16/18 E7表位肽,这些表位肽被小鼠H-2 I/II类分子限制。通过流式细胞术、ELISA和Western blotting,在体外利用骨髓来源的树突状细胞(BMDC)刺激实验中合成并评估了Ii-Key修饰的MHC II类肽(LRMK-PEG2-表位)和未修饰的MHC I类肽。通过淋巴器官免疫表型分析和血浆细胞因子谱分析,在C57BL/6小鼠中评估了其体内免疫原性。在早期干预的皮下TC-1肿瘤模型(HPV16 E6/E7阳性)中测试了抗肿瘤活性,通过组织病理学分析和肿瘤浸润淋巴细胞的流式细胞术分析进行评估。还评估了治疗与抗PD-1单克隆抗体的联合治疗效果。结果 肽池促进了BMDC成熟,表现为CD80+CD86+和I-A/I-E+ BMDC频率增加、NF-κB通路激活以及促炎细胞因子分泌增加,这些指标表明树突状细胞激活。在TC-1模型中,肽治疗抑制了肿瘤生长并定性减少了肿瘤Ki67染色,伴随肿瘤内CD4+和CD8+ T细胞频率增加的非显著趋势。与抗PD-1联合使用可实现比单用更佳的肿瘤控制效果。通过组织病理学和血清生化评估的安全性分析表明,在所测试的条件和观察期内耐受性良好。结论 含Ii-Key的HPV16/18 E7肽制剂促进了树突状细胞激活和T细胞免疫,在早期干预的TC-1模型中表现出可接受的耐受性下的抗肿瘤活性。与抗PD-1联合使用比单用更能有效控制肿瘤,但这种比较并未证明其具有加成或协同效应。这些临床前研究结果支持进一步评估该制剂,包括直接抗原呈递实验和匹配的未修饰MHC-II肽对照。

title: Neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in human papillomavirus–negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a review
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) has a substantial risk of recurrence despite multimodal treatment. Mutation-derived neoepitopes provide a rationale for personalized vaccination, but their clinical relevance depends on target expression and clonality, effective antigen presentation, and access of functional T cells to malignant cells. This narrative review distinguishes direct HPV-negative HNSCC evidence from HNSCC-inclusive programs, shared-antigen comparators, target-selection technologies, and cross-tumor studies. The randomized phase I TG4050 study in 33 patients with resected HPV-negative HNSCC supports feasibility and immunogenicity; its small sample, few recurrence events, and per-protocol recurrence analysis preclude definitive efficacy conclusions. Complementary translational and cross-tumor studies inform antigen selection, vaccine delivery, and combination strategies, with uncertain transferability to HPV-negative HNSCC. We examine the separate evidentiary requirements for predicted targets, natural human leukocyte antigen (HLA) presentation, T-cell recognition, tumor-cell killing, and clinical benefit. We discuss spatial immune profiling to investigate resistance and circulating tumor DNA to monitor disease, while emphasizing that their roles in guiding vaccination remain exploratory. Future studies should define the treatment setting, evaluate whether vaccination adds benefit to contemporary standard treatment, report manufacturing attrition and time to first dose, and connect standardized immune measurements with clinical outcomes. Personalized neoepitope vaccination remains investigational in HPV-negative HNSCC, and adequately powered randomized trials are required to establish its clinical role.

title_original: Neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in human papillomavirus–negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a review

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the use of neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The central question is whether these vaccines can improve outcomes in HPV-negative HNSCC, given the substantial risk of recurrence despite multimodal treatment.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with a specific emphasis on the TG4050 randomized phase I study in 33 patients with resected HPV-negative HNSCC. The study supports the feasibility and immunogenicity of personalized neoepitope vaccination but lacks sufficient data to draw definitive efficacy conclusions due to its small sample size, few recurrence events, and per-protocol analysis. The review also highlights the need for adequately powered randomized trials to establish the clinical role of neoepitope vaccination in HPV-negative HNSCC.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mutation-derived neoepitopes offer a rationale for personalized vaccination in HPV-negative HNSCC, but their clinical relevance depends on factors such as target expression, clonality, antigen presentation, and T-cell functionality. It also emphasizes that while complementary translational and cross-tumor studies provide insights into antigen selection, vaccine delivery, and combination strategies, their transferability to HPV-negative HNSCC remains uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on the efficacy of neoepitope-based vaccines in HPV-negative HNSCC, with the TG4050 study being too small to provide conclusive results. title_zh: 基于新表位的癌症疫苗在HPV阴性头颈鳞状细胞癌中的应用:综述
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) has a substantial risk of recurrence despite multimodal treatment. Mutation-derived neoepitopes provide a rationale for personalized vaccination, but their clinical relevance depends on target expression and clonality, effective antigen presentation, and access of functional T cells to malignant cells. This narrative review distinguishes direct HPV-negative HNSCC evidence from HNSCC-inclusive programs, shared-antigen comparators, target-selection technologies, and cross-tumor studies. The randomized phase I TG4050 study in 33 patients with resected HPV-negative HNSCC supports feasibility and immunogenicity; its small sample, few recurrence events, and per-protocol recurrence analysis preclude definitive efficacy conclusions. Complementary translational and cross-tumor studies inform antigen selection, vaccine delivery, and combination strategies, with uncertain transferability to HPV-negative HNSCC. We examine the separate evidentiary requirements for predicted targets, natural human leukocyte antigen (HLA) presentation, T-cell recognition, tumor-cell killing, and clinical benefit. We discuss spatial immune profiling to investigate resistance and circulating tumor DNA to monitor disease, while emphasizing that their roles in guiding vaccination remain exploratory. Future studies should define the treatment setting, evaluate whether vaccination adds benefit to contemporary standard treatment, report manufacturing attrition and time to first dose, and connect standardized immune measurements with clinical outcomes. Personalized neoepitope vaccination remains investigational in HPV-negative HNSCC, and adequately powered randomized trials are required to establish its clinical role.
abstract_zh: HPV阴性的头颈鳞状细胞癌(HNSCC)即使经过多模式治疗治疗,仍具有显著的复发风险。由突变衍生的新表位为个性化疫苗接种提供了理论依据,但其临床相关性取决于靶点表达和克隆性、有效的抗原呈递以及功能性T细胞能否到达恶性细胞。本叙述性综述区分了直接HPV阴性HNSCC证据与HNSCC包容性项目、共享抗原对照组、靶点选择技术以及跨肿瘤研究。在33名接受手术切除的HPV阴性HNSCC患者中进行的随机I期TG4050研究支持了个性化新表位疫苗接种的可行性与免疫原性;然而,由于样本量小、复发事件少以及按协议分析,尚无法得出明确的疗效结论。互补的转化研究和跨肿瘤研究为抗原选择、疫苗递送以及联合策略提供了信息,但其在HPV阴性HNSCC中的可转移性仍不确定。我们探讨了预测靶点、自然人类白细胞抗原(HLA)呈递、T细胞识别、肿瘤细胞杀伤以及临床获益所需的独立证据。我们讨论了空间免疫分析以研究耐药性以及循环肿瘤DNA以监测疾病,同时强调这些方法在指导疫苗接种中的作用仍处于探索阶段。未来的研究应定义治疗的适用场景,评估疫苗接种是否能为当前标准治疗带来额外益处,报告制造过程中的损耗和首次给药时间,并将标准化的免疫测量与临床结果联系起来。基于新表位的疫苗接种在HPV阴性HNSCC中仍处于研究阶段,需要足够样本量的随机试验来确立其临床作用。

title: Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: HPV16 and Grade as Recurrence Predictors in a 10-Year Series.
abstract: Abstract Objectives: To characterize the clinical profile, treatment patterns and factors associated with high-grade recurrence in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) at a tertiary referral center over 10 years. Methods: Retrospective single-center cohort (2013–2023) of 71 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed VaIN. Primary outcome: histologically confirmed high-grade recurrence or progression (HSIL+: VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma); VaIN1 on follow-up was not considered recurrence. Results: Mean age 47.9±10.5 years. Index grade: VaIN1/LSIL 59.2%, VaIN2 32.4%, VaIN3 8.5%. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% and HPV16 in 22.5%; 52.8% of genotyped patients had multiple infections. Over a median follow-up of 48 months [IQR 36–84], 12 patients (16.9%) developed HSIL+ (VaIN2 n=10, VaIN3 n=1, carcinoma n=1); median time to event was 14.5 months [IQR 8.8–27.5]; 24-month HSIL+-free probability was 88%. HPV16-positive patients had shorter HSIL+-free survival (log-rank p=0.046), although the crude difference in HSIL+ rates was not significant (31.3% vs 12.7%; OR 3.12, 95% CI 0.83–11.69; p=0.125). Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend (27.6% vs 9.5%; OR 3.62, 95% CI 0.97–13.46; p=0.059). Conclusions: In this series, HPV16 was associated with earlier high-grade recurrence, and index HSIL showed a consistent but non-significant trend. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by 12 events, support prospective evaluation of genotype- and grade-based surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the clinical profile, treatment patterns and factors associated with high-grade recurrence in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) over a 10-year period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted from 2013 to 2023, including 71 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed VaIN.
analysis.methods: The primary outcome was histologically confirmed high-grade recurrence or progression (HSIL+: VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma), with VaIN1 on follow-up not considered recurrence. The study analyzed HPV genotypes and their association with recurrence outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The mean age was 47.9±10.5 years. Index grades were VaIN1/LSIL in 59.2%, VaIN2 in 32.4%, and VaIN3 in 8.5%. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% of patients, with HPV16 identified in 22.5% and 52.8% having multiple infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HPV16-positive patients had shorter HSIL+-free survival, although the crude difference in HSIL+ rates was not statistically significant. Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend towards higher recurrence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that HPV16 and the initial grade of VaIN may be important factors in predicting high-grade recurrence, which could inform more targeted surveillance strategies for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small number of events (12) and a non-significant trend in some results, which may affect the strength of the conclusions. However, the hypothesis-generating nature of the findings supports further prospective evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical profile, treatment patterns, and recurrence predictors in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) over a 10-year period at a tertiary referral center. The primary outcome was high-grade recurrence or progression, defined as HSIL+ (VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma). The study found that HPV16 positivity was associated with earlier recurrence, although the difference was not statistically significant. Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend towards higher recurrence. The mean age of participants was 47.9±10.5 years, with the majority having VaIN1/LSIL. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% of patients, and 52.8% had multiple infections. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by a small number of events, suggest the need for prospective evaluation of genotype- and grade-based surveillance strategies for HPV-associated diseases.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the clinical profile, treatment patterns and factors associated with high-grade recurrence in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) over a 10-year period.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted from 2013 to 2023, including 71 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed VaIN.
analysis_en.methods: The primary outcome was histologically confirmed high-grade recurrence or progression (HSIL+: VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma), with VaIN1 on follow-up not considered recurrence. The study analyzed HPV genotypes and their association with recurrence outcomes.
analysis_en.main_results: The mean age was 47.9±10.5 years. Index grades were VaIN1/LSIL in 59.2%, VaIN2 in 32.4%, and VaIN3 in 8.5%. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% of patients, with HPV16 identified in 22.5% and 52.8% having multiple infections.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HPV16-positive patients had shorter HSIL+-free survival, although the crude difference in HSIL+ rates was not statistically significant. Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend towards higher recurrence.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that HPV16 and the initial grade of VaIN may be important factors in predicting high-grade recurrence, which could inform more targeted surveillance strategies for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small number of events (12) and a non-significant trend in some results, which may affect the strength of the conclusions. However, the hypothesis-generating nature of the findings supports further prospective evaluation.

title_zh: 阴道上皮内瘤变:HPV16和初始分级作为10年系列中复发的预测因子。
source_body_en: Abstract Objectives: To characterize the clinical profile, treatment patterns and factors associated with high-grade recurrence in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) at a tertiary referral center over 10 years. Methods: Retrospective single-center cohort (2013–2023) of 71 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed VaIN. Primary outcome: histologically confirmed high-grade recurrence or progression (HSIL+: VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma); VaIN1 on follow-up was not considered recurrence. Results: Mean age 47.9±10.5 years. Index grade: VaIN1/LSIL 59.2%, VaIN2 32.4%, VaIN3 8.5%. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% and HPV16 in 22.5%; 52.8% of genotyped patients had multiple infections. Over a median follow-up of 48 months [IQR 36–84], 12 patients (16.9%) developed HSIL+ (VaIN2 n=10, VaIN3 n=1, carcinoma n=1); median time to event was 14.5 months [IQR 8.8–27.5]; 24-month HSIL+-free probability was 88%. HPV16-positive patients had shorter HSIL+-free survival (log-rank p=0.046), although the crude difference in HSIL+ rates was not significant (31.3% vs 12.7%; OR 3.12, 95% CI 0.83–11.69; p=0.125). Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend (27.6% vs 9.5%; OR 3.62, 95% CI 0.97–13.46; p=0.059). Conclusions: In this series, HPV16 was associated with earlier high-grade recurrence, and index HSIL showed a consistent but non-significant trend. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by 12 events, support prospective evaluation of genotype- and grade-based surveillance.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述在10年期间患有阴道上皮内瘤变(VaIN)的患者中,高危复发的临床特征、治疗模式及相关因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项从2013年至2023年的回顾性单中心队列研究研究,包括71例经组织学确诊的VaIN患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 主要结局是经组织学确诊的高危复发或进展(HSIL+:VaIN2–3或浸润性癌),随访中出现的VaIN1不被视为复发。研究分析了HPV基因型及其与复发结局的关系。
analysis_zh.main_results: 平均年龄为47.9±10.5岁。初始分级中,VaIN1/LSIL占59.2%,VaIN2占32.4%,VaIN3占8.5%。高危型HPV在71.8%的患者中被检测到,其中HPV16占22.5%,52.8%的患者存在多重感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,HPV16阳性患者的HSIL+-无复发生存期较短,尽管HSIL+率的粗略差异不具有统计学意义。初始HSIL显示出向更高复发率发展的非显著趋势。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,HPV16和VaIN的初始分级可能是预测高危复发的重要因素,这可能有助于制定更针对性的监测策略,以应对HPV相关疾病。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于事件数量较少(12个)以及某些结果中的非显著趋势,这可能影响结论的强度。然而,这些产生假设的发现支持进一步的前瞻性评估。

title: HPV Infection in Sub-Saharan Africa: Circulating Genotypes, Vaccination Strategies (Single-Dose Versus Two-Dose), and Implications of HIV Co-Infection
abstract: Cervical cancer is a major cause of morbidity and mortality among women in sub-Saharan Africa, where vaccination coverage remains below the World Health Organization target of 90% of girls fully vaccinated by 15 years of age. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype distribution, single-dose versus two-dose vaccination, and the implications of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Although HPV 16 and HPV 18 remain the predominant oncogenic types, HPV 35, HPV 52, HPV 45, HPV 33, and HPV 58 are reported frequently in sub-Saharan African populations. Consequently, some high-risk infections fall outside bivalent and quadrivalent vaccine coverage, and some detected types remain outside nonavalent vaccine coverage. Randomized trials in Tanzania and Kenya demonstrate durable single-dose immunogenicity through 60 months and vaccine efficacy above 98% against persistent vaccine-type infection through 54 months, respectively. A trial in Costa Rica provides a direct five-year randomized comparison showing non-inferiority of one dose to two doses. Equivalent single-dose efficacy and durability evidence for people living with HIV remains unavailable. These findings support expanded single-dose vaccination in immunocompetent populations alongside multidose pathways for people living with HIV, genotype-specific surveillance, and continued cervical screening.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically examining circulating genotypes, vaccination strategies (single-dose versus two-dose), and the implications of HIV co-infection in sub-Saharan Africa. The central question is whether single-dose vaccination is as effective as two-dose regimens in preventing HPV-related diseases, particularly in immunocompetent populations and those living with HIV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing evidence, drawing on randomized trials conducted in Tanzania, Kenya, and Costa Rica. It includes studies on HPV genotype distribution, vaccine efficacy, and immunogenicity. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but relies on direct comparisons and observational data.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV 16 and HPV 18 remain the predominant oncogenic types in sub-Saharan Africa, although other high-risk types such as HPV 35, HPV 52, HPV 45, HPV 33, and HPV 58 are also frequently reported. Single-dose vaccination has demonstrated durable immunogenicity and high efficacy against persistent vaccine-type infections, with evidence from trials in Tanzania and Kenya showing efficacy above 98% over 54 months. A Costa Rican trial also found non-inferiority of one dose compared to two doses over five years.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of direct evidence on the efficacy and durability of single-dose HPV vaccination in people living with HIV. While immunogenicity and efficacy data are available for immunocompetent populations, these findings cannot be directly transferred to HIV-positive individuals due to the absence of target-specific studies. Additionally, some high-risk HPV infections fall outside the coverage of bivalent and quadrivalent vaccines, and certain types remain outside nonavalent vaccine coverage.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that single-dose vaccination should be expanded in immunocompetent populations, while multidose vaccination pathways should be maintained for people living with HIV. There is a need for genotype-specific surveillance and continued cervical screening to address the gaps in vaccine coverage and to monitor the effectiveness of vaccination strategies in the region.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on circulating genotypes, vaccination strategies, and the impact of HIV co-infection. It highlights that HPV 16 and HPV 18 are the most prevalent oncogenic types, though other high-risk variants are also common. Single-dose vaccination has shown high efficacy and durability in immunocompetent populations, supported by trials in Tanzania, Kenya, and Costa Rica. However, evidence for single-dose efficacy in people living with HIV is lacking. The review recommends expanded single-dose vaccination alongside multidose pathways for HIV-positive individuals, genotype-specific surveillance, and continued cervical screening to address gaps in vaccine coverage and improve public health outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV),具体分析了在撒哈拉以南非洲地区流行的基因型、疫苗接种接种策略(单剂与双剂)以及HIV共感染的影响。核心问题是:在免疫功能正常人群和HIV感染者中,单剂疫苗接种是否与双剂接种方案在预防HPV相关疾病方面同样有效。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是现有证据的叙述性综合,基于在坦桑尼亚、肯尼亚和哥斯达黎加进行的随机对照试验。它包括关于HPV基因型分布、疫苗疫苗有效性和免疫原性的研究。综述未报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是依赖直接比较和观察性数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV 16和HPV 18仍然是撒哈拉以南非洲地区的主要致癌型,尽管其他高危型如HPV 35、HPV 52、HPV 45、HPV 33和HPV 58也被频繁报告。在坦桑尼亚和肯尼亚的试验中,单剂疫苗接种已显示出在60个月内具有持久的免疫原性,并且在54个月内对持续性疫苗型感染的有效性超过98%。哥斯达黎加的一项试验也发现,单剂与双剂在五年内的预防效果具有非劣性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 对于HIV感染者而言,关于单剂HPV 疫苗接种在预防效果和持久性方面的直接证据仍然缺乏。虽然免疫原性和有效性数据在免疫功能正常人群中已有,但由于缺乏针对特定类型的试验,这些发现不能直接应用于HIV感染者。此外,一些高危型HPV感染类型超出了二价和四价疫苗的覆盖范围,而某些类型仍不在九价疫苗的覆盖范围内。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现表明,应在免疫功能正常人群中扩大单剂疫苗接种接种,同时在HIV感染者中维持多剂接种路径。需要针对特定基因型进行监测,并继续进行宫颈癌筛查,以弥补疫苗覆盖范围的不足,并监测该地区疫苗接种策略的有效性。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV),具体分析了在撒哈拉以南非洲地区流行的基因型、疫苗接种接种策略(单剂与双剂)以及HIV共感染的影响。核心问题是:在免疫功能正常人群和HIV感染者中,单剂疫苗接种是否与双剂接种方案在预防HPV相关疾病方面同样有效。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是现有证据的叙述性综合,基于在坦桑尼亚、肯尼亚和哥斯达黎加进行的随机对照试验。它包括关于HPV基因型分布、疫苗疫苗有效性和免疫原性的研究。综述未报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是依赖直接比较和观察性数据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV 16和HPV 18仍然是撒哈拉以南非洲地区的主要致癌型,尽管其他高危型如HPV 35、HPV 52、HPV 45、HPV 33和HPV 58也被频繁报告。在坦桑尼亚和肯尼亚的试验中,单剂疫苗接种已显示出在60个月内具有持久的免疫原性,并且在54个月内对持续性疫苗型感染的有效性超过98%。哥斯达黎加的一项试验也发现,单剂与双剂在五年内的预防效果具有非劣性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 对于HIV感染者而言,关于单剂HPV 疫苗接种在预防效果和持久性方面的直接证据仍然缺乏。虽然免疫原性和有效性数据在免疫功能正常人群中已有,但由于缺乏针对特定类型的试验,这些发现不能直接应用于HIV感染者。此外,一些高危型HPV感染类型超出了二价和四价疫苗的覆盖范围,而某些类型仍不在九价疫苗的覆盖范围内。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现表明,应在免疫功能正常人群中扩大单剂疫苗接种接种,同时在HIV感染者中维持多剂接种路径。需要针对特定基因型进行监测,并继续进行宫颈癌筛查,以弥补疫苗覆盖范围的不足,并监测该地区疫苗接种策略的有效性。

title: The Association of Oral and Anogenital Human Papillomavirus Genotypes With Head and Neck Cancers in Brazil: A Nationwide Case-Control Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT This multicenter case–control study assessed (2019–2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer‐free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50–65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high‐risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV‐16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV‐16/18–positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case–control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high‐risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten‐fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92–34.6). Oral HPV‐16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52–26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site‐specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV‐16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil, addressing the need to understand the role of HPV in these cancers.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A nationwide case-control study conducted between 2019 and 2023, involving 314 participants (157 cases and 157 controls), mostly males aged 50–65 years.
analysis_en.methods: Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping, and associations were estimated using conditional regression.
analysis_en.main_results: Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), with HPV-16/18 more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case–control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma, highlighting its potential role in this disease.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that oral HPV-16/18 may be a significant risk factor for head and neck cancers, particularly oropharyngeal carcinoma, which could inform targeted screening and prevention strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a relatively small sample size and relied on self-reported data, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of a matched case-control design and central laboratory processing.

title_zh: 巴西口腔及肛生殖器人乳头瘤病毒基因型与头颈癌的关联:一项全国性病例对照研究。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT This multicenter case–control study assessed (2019–2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer‐free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50–65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high‐risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV‐16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV‐16/18–positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case–control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high‐risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten‐fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92–34.6). Oral HPV‐16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52–26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site‐specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV‐16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract_zh: 摘要 本多中心病例对照研究(2019–2023年)评估了巴西口腔及肛生殖器人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)基因型与头颈癌的关联。纳入病例为18岁及以上新诊断、组织学确认的口腔、口咽、下咽或喉部鳞状细胞癌患者。对照组(无癌症个体)按地区、性别和年龄进行后验匹配。口腔、生殖器和肛门样本在中央实验室进行HPV基因型检测。采用条件回归模型估计关联。分析包括314名参与者(157名病例,157名对照),其中大部分为男性(79%),年龄在50–65岁之间(51%)。口腔HPV 患病率在病例和对照组中相似(14% vs. 12%),主要涉及高危型基因型(40种中有35种)。病例中HPV-16/18感染率更高(7.3% vs. 1.9%;p = 0.024),其中大多数HPV-16/18阳性癌症位于口咽部(11例中有10例)。生殖器HPV 患病率感染率为39%,无病例对照差异,而肛门HPV 患病率感染率为17%。病例中任何高危型肛门HPV感染的比例高于对照组(16% vs. 最小的基因型一致性在口腔和肛生殖器部位之间观察到。当前吸烟者作为病例的几率是对照组的十倍(调整后OR 10.0;95% CI 2.92–34.6)。口腔HPV-16/18感染与头颈癌独立相关(调整后OR 6.30;95% CI 1.52–26.1)。多部位HPV基因型检测揭示了特定部位的定植模式,生殖器感染在男女中最为普遍。经过多变量调整后,仅口腔HPV-16/18感染与头颈癌有显著关联,尤其是口咽癌。

title: Social Media Insights Into the Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Catch-Up Campaign for Young Adults in the Netherlands, 2023-2024: Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but its uptake remains suboptimal. In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited individuals aged 18 to 27 years for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV vaccination in 2023‐2024, which led to 24% of the invited population getting vaccinated. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns, and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts. In addition to the overall evaluation of the vaccination campaign, we piloted online social listening processes to generate an insight report for the Public Health Service (PHS) Amsterdam. Objective This study piloted online social listening processes at PHS Amsterdam to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign among young adults. Methods Following an inventory of potential platforms and data sources, a retrospective online social listening analysis was conducted across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter), using data from PHS Amsterdam, the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, the Dutch public broadcasting foundation, and LINDA.meiden from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024. Publicly available posts, comments, and engagement concerning HPV vaccination were manually collected and inductively coded. Themes were assessed for risk based on expected potential harm and observed reach and were used to develop recommendations. Results A total of 821 posts and 5157 comments were collected and analyzed. Ten recurring themes were identified across varying risk levels. Two themes were classified as high risk: an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about the transparency regarding HPV vaccine side effects. Three themes were classified as medium risk: questioning HPV vaccine effectiveness, reduced general vaccine trust following COVID-19, and accessibility issues related to vaccination locations and service times. Two themes were classified as neutral risk: questions regarding campaign eligibility criteria and calls for broader HPV prevention measures. Finally, 3 low-risk themes concerned questions regarding HPV vaccine brand specifics, campaign choices, and scheduling HPV appointments. Comments also referred to subsequent information sources, including reliable sources, false narratives, and misinformation. Recommendations focused on addressing questions and information gaps (ie, improving risk perception and providing more detailed HPV vaccine information), improving communication, and reducing practical barriers to vaccination. Conclusions Manual social listening across selected online sources provided actionable insights into the public discourse during the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign. Results mostly reflected questions, concerns, and information gaps. Although some themes were critical of HPV vaccination, false narratives and misinformation did not dominate the discourse. Recommendations aim to reduce practical barriers and address information needs. This pilot showed that online social listening can be effectively implemented even with limited resources.

source_records.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but its uptake remains suboptimal. In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited individuals aged 18 to 27 years for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV vaccination in 2023-2024, which led to 24% of the invited population getting vaccinated. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns, and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts. In addition to the overall evaluation of the vaccination campaign, we piloted online social listening processes to generate an insight report for the Public Health Service (PHS) Amsterdam. Objective This study piloted online social listening processes at PHS Amsterdam to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign among young adults. Methods Following an inventory of potential platforms and data sources, a retrospective online social listening analysis was conducted across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter), using data from PHS Amsterdam, the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, the Dutch public broadcasting foundation, and LINDA.meiden from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024. Publicly available posts, comments, and engagement concerning HPV vaccination were manually collected and inductively coded. Themes were assessed for risk based on expected potential harm and observed reach and were used to develop recommendations. Results A total of 821 posts and 5157 comments were collected and analyzed. Ten recurring themes were identified across varying risk levels. Two themes were classified as high risk: an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about the transparency regarding HPV vaccine side effects. Three themes were classified as medium risk: questioning HPV vaccine effectiveness, reduced general vaccine trust following COVID-19, and accessibility issues related to vaccination locations and service times. Two themes were classified as neutral risk: questions regarding campaign eligibility criteria and calls for broader HPV prevention measures. Finally, 3 low-risk themes concerned questions regarding HPV vaccine brand specifics, campaign choices, and scheduling HPV appointments. Comments also referred to subsequent information sources, including reliable sources, false narratives, and misinformation. Recommendations focused on addressing questions and information gaps (ie, improving risk perception and providing more detailed HPV vaccine information), improving communication, and reducing practical barriers to vaccination. Conclusions Manual social listening across selected online sources provided actionable insights into the public discourse during the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign. Results mostly reflected questions, concerns, and information gaps. Although some themes were critical of HPV vaccination, false narratives and misinformation did not dominate the discourse. Recommendations aim to reduce practical barriers and address information needs. This pilot showed that online social listening can be effectively implemented even with limited resources.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在荷兰,一项补种活动于2023-2024年邀请了18至27岁的人群,提供额外的免费接种机会,使24%的受邀人群接种了疫苗。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能通过突出需要解决HPV疫苗有效性及副作用的错误信息和信息缺口,为未来的HPV疫苗接种工作提供信息。它们还表明了改善沟通和减少HPV疫苗接种实践障碍的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于依赖手动收集和编码的社交媒体数据,这可能引入偏差。由于研究基于资源和范围有限的试点,其证据强度为中等。

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women. METHODS: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection. RESULTS: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic between 2018 and 2019. A total of 1302 asymptomatic women were enrolled, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and HPV detection using PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit. The results showed that 21.6% of participants tested positive for HPV, with types 52, 58, and 16 being the most prevalent. Overall, 9.0% of women had abnormal cytology, and 0.2% had cervical cancer. Multivariable analysis revealed that older women and those from Luangprabang province had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology. Single/divorced/widow women were more likely to test positive for HPV compared to married women. The study highlights the importance of HPV genotypes 52, 58, and 16 in cervical cancer risk and advocates for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. The findings suggest that periodic screening should be considered for women too old to benefit from the vaccine.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌是全球女性中常见的疾病原因和死亡率,并且与高危型(HR)人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)基因型的存在有强烈关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2018年10月至2019年2月期间,邀请了来自Xiengkhouang、Luangprabang、Oudomxay和Huaphan省的1302名无症状女性(平均年龄37.4岁,年龄范围18-76岁)填写问卷,并采集宫颈细胞进行细胞学检查,同时采集拭子用于PCR和AnyplexTM II HPV-HR检测。
elements_zh.methods: AnyplexTM II HPV-HR试剂盒在1184名参与者中检测出256例阳性(21.6%),其中最常见的高危型基因型为52型(20.4%)、58型(12.8%)和16型(11.7%)。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,在1268名具有可评估样本的女性中,有114人(9.0%)细胞学结果异常,3人(0.2%)患有宫颈癌。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多变量分析显示,年龄≥40岁的参与者(OR:1.6;95% CI:1.1-2.4,p = 0.015)以及居住在Luangprabang省的参与者(OR:1.9;95% CI:1.1-3.2,p = 0.02)比年轻女性和居住在Huaphan省的女性更可能有异常细胞学结果。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HPV 52、58和16型是最常见的高危型基因型,这清楚地表明应引入九价疫苗。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单身、离婚或丧偶的女性比已婚女性更可能检测到HPV(OR:2.3;95% CI:1.5-3.7,p < 0.001)。

abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌是全球女性中导致发病率和死亡率的常见原因,并且与高危型(HR)人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)基因型的存在有强烈关联。本研究旨在确定Lao女性中HPV的患病率及其基因型,并探讨其与细胞学检查结果的关系。方法:2018年10月至2019年2月期间,邀请了来自Xiengkhouang、Luangprabang、Oudomxay和Huaphan省的1302名无症状女性(平均年龄37.4岁,年龄范围18-76岁)填写问卷,并采集宫颈细胞进行细胞学检查,以及采集拭子用于PCR和AnyplexTM II HPV-HR检测。结果:总体而言,1268名可评估样本的女性中有114人(9.0%)细胞学检查结果异常,3人(0.2%)患有宫颈癌。AnyplexTM II HPV-HR试剂盒在1184名参与者中检测出256例阳性(21.6%),其中最常见的高危型基因型为52型(20.4%)、58型(12.8%)和16型(11.7%)。多变量分析显示,年龄≥40岁的参与者(OR:1.6;95% CI:1.1-2.4,p = 0.015)以及居住在Luangprabang省的参与者(OR:1.9;95% CI:1.1-3.2,p = 0.02)比年轻女性和居住在Huaphan省的女性更可能有异常细胞学检查结果。单身、离婚或丧偶的女性比已婚女性更可能检测到HPV(OR:2.3;95% CI:1.5-3.7,p < 0.001)。结论:HPV 52、58和16型是最常见的高危型基因型,这清楚地表明应引入非十价疫苗。对于年龄太大而无法从最近引入的疫苗中受益的女性,应考虑定期筛查。

title: Determinants of human papillomavirus vaccine uptake among ​​Iranian adults: a nationally representative survey using the Iranian HPV ​Vaccine Determinants Scale (I-HPV-VDS)
abstract: Human ​papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a major global public health burden. Despite the availability of effective vaccines, clear national policies on HPV vaccination remain absent in Iran. Understanding current HPV vaccine coverage and the factors influencing vaccine acceptance among Iranian adults is essential for guiding effective public health interventions. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 using an online survey of Iranian adults. We utilized the newly developed Iranian HPV Vaccine Determinants Scale (I-HPV-VDS), which was constructed based on well-established health behavior frameworks. Psychometric assessment of the questionnaire included using face validity, construct validity, and Cronbach’s alpha. Post-stratification weighting was applied using national distributions of age, gender and educational attainment to improve population representativeness. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify determinants of HPV vaccine uptake. In the weighted sample of 1416 Iranian adults, HPV vaccine uptake was 5.5%. Vaccine uptake was significantly higher among younger adults (aOR: 2.88, 95% CI: 1.52–5.47), females (aOR: 5.90, 95% CI: 3.09–11.26), and unmarried individuals (aOR: 16.72, 95% CI: 7.64–36.57), particularly those previously married or in non-marital relationships. Each one standard deviation increase in Social Support and Self-efficacy was associated with nearly 4 times higher odds of uptake (aOR: 4.46, 95% CI: 2.43–8.18), while Risk Perception was associated with about 2 times higher odds (aOR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.27–3.52). Interestingly, stigma-related and behavioral concern components were not independently associated with vaccination in multivariable analysis. It is of note that the wide CIs observed for several subgroups likely reflect very low event counts in specific strata combined with post-stratification weighting, which warrants cautious interpretation of these findings. The critically low HPV vaccination uptake, particularly in men, alongside profound social inequities suggest a need to consider measures to improve access, including possible inclusion of the HPV vaccine in the nation​al immunization program. Furthermore, considering recent HPV vaccination initiatives in neighboring countries and the central role of HPV vaccination in global cervical cancer elimination efforts, strengthening public understanding of HPV susceptibility and vaccine effectiveness, as well as enhancing supportive social environments within the Iranian context is essential.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究调查了伊朗成年人中人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种的决定因素,重点关注影响接受率和覆盖率的因素。核心问题是识别疫苗接种的关键决定因素,并了解当前HPV 疫苗接种在人群中的状况。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次回顾是一项于2025年进行的横断面研究,通过在线调查伊朗成年人完成。研究设计包括问卷的心理测量评估,包括表面效度、结构效度和Cronbach’s alpha。应用事后分层加权以提高人口代表性。采用单变量和多变量逻辑回归分析来识别HPV 疫苗接种的决定因素。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在加权样本中,有1416名伊朗成年人,HPV 疫苗接种率为5.5%。与较高接种率显著相关的因素包括较年轻年龄、女性性别和未婚状态。此外,较高的社会支持和自我效能水平与疫苗接种率增加相关,而风险感知也显示出正相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,在多变量分析中,与污名相关的和行为担忧成分并未独立与疫苗接种相关。某些亚组的宽置信区间表明,由于特定层面上事件数量非常少,结合事后分层加权,需要谨慎解释这些亚组特定的结果。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: HPV 疫苗接种接种率极低,尤其是在男性中,这表明需要采取措施提高接种可及性,例如将HPV 疫苗纳入国家免疫计划。加强公众对HPV易感性和疫苗有效性的理解,并在伊朗背景下改善支持性社会环境,对于提高HPV 疫苗接种接种率至关重要。

title: Cervical cancer risk reduction in the era of human papillomavirus vaccination.
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination status is important to consider when evaluating the population‐level impact of cervical screening uptake on cervical cancer risk, yet screening rates are rarely presented by vaccination status, limiting assessments of population‐level protection against cervical cancer. Methods Using females 21–39 years old from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey ( N = 4000), the authors report the proportion up‐to‐date with cervical screening stratified by age and self‐reported HPV vaccination status. Using assumptions of 85% and 70% reduction in cervical cancer risk from HPV vaccination and up‐to‐date screening status, respectively, the authors explore the population‐level reduction in cervical cancer risk from varying screening coverage by HPV vaccination status. Results A total of 78.4% of females were up‐to‐date with screening, 38.0% reported ever receiving an HPV vaccine, and 15.3% were both unvaccinated and not up‐to‐date with screening. Across age groups, the proportion of females up‐to‐date with screening was 6.3%–19.1% higher for vaccinated versus unvaccinated females. The relative reduction in cervical cancer risk from vaccination and screening ranged from 62.1% for females 36–39 years old to 73.1% for females 26–30 years old, compared to the absence of vaccination and screening. Despite females 21–25 years old having the lowest screening uptake, their reduction in cervical cancer risk was not the lowest due to higher vaccination levels. Conclusions Cervical screening rates are higher among females who were vaccinated against HPV, resulting in a higher population‐level risk of cervical cancer than expected from considering vaccination and screening rates independently. Including vaccination status in national surveillance data sets would help identify and target interventions within communities at higher risk.

They emphasize the importance of including vaccination status in surveillance data to better target interventions in high-risk communities. The study's findings are based on survey data and assumptions about risk reduction, which may introduce limitations. The evidence is considered moderate due to the reliance on self-reported information and the absence of direct biological measurements.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在评估宫颈筛查参与对宫颈癌风险的群体影响时,需要考虑HPV(人乳头瘤病毒)疫苗接种状态,但筛查率很少按疫苗接种状态进行报告,限制了对群体层面宫颈癌保护效果的评估。方法 使用2019年国家健康访谈调查中21–39岁女性的数据(N = 4000),作者报告了按年龄和自述HPV 疫苗接种状态分层的宫颈筛查参与比例。通过假设HPV 疫苗接种和及时筛查状态分别将宫颈癌风险降低85%和70%,作者探讨了不同筛查覆盖率下宫颈癌风险的群体层面降低情况。结果 总共有78.4%的女性及时接受了筛查,38.0%的女性报告曾接受过HPV 疫苗,15.3%的女性既未接种疫苗也未及时接受筛查。在不同年龄组中,接种疫苗的女性及时接受筛查的比例比未接种疫苗的女性高出6.3%–19.1%。接种HPV 疫苗接种和及时筛查对宫颈癌风险的相对降低范围从36–39岁女性的62.1%到26–30岁女性的73.1%,与未接种HPV 疫苗接种且未及时筛查的情况相比。尽管21–25岁女性的筛查参与率最低,但由于其HPV 疫苗接种水平较高,其宫颈癌风险降低幅度并非最低。结论 接种过HPV疫苗的女性宫颈筛查率更高,导致宫颈癌风险的群体层面降低幅度高于仅考虑HPV 疫苗接种和筛查率独立情况的预期值。将HPV 疫苗接种状态纳入国家监测数据集有助于识别和针对高风险社区进行干预。

analysis_zh.methods: 作者分析了2019年国家健康访谈调查的数据,以报告按年龄和自述HPV 疫苗接种状态分层的宫颈筛查参与比例。他们假设HPV 疫苗接种和及时筛查状态分别将宫颈癌风险降低85%和70%,以探讨不同筛查覆盖率下宫颈癌风险的群体层面降低情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,78.4%的女性及时接受了筛查,38.0%的女性报告曾接受过HPV 疫苗,15.3%的女性既未接种疫苗也未及时接受筛查。在不同年龄组中,接种疫苗的女性及时接受筛查的比例比未接种疫苗的女性高出6.3%–19.1%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,接种过HPV疫苗的女性宫颈筛查率更高,导致宫颈癌风险的群体层面降低幅度高于仅考虑HPV 疫苗接种和筛查率独立情况的预期值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,将HPV 疫苗接种状态纳入国家监测数据集有助于识别和针对高风险社区进行干预,从而改善宫颈癌的预防策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于依赖自述数据,未考虑潜在的偏倚或混杂因素。证据强度中等,因为它是基于调查数据而非直接的临床或生物学测量。

title: CRISPR/Cas-Enabled Point-of-Care Screening of Human Papillomavirus in Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistent infection, particularly involving high-risk subtypes, remains the primary driver of cervical cancer, underlining the exigent need for rapid, accessible point-of-care (POC) diagnostics. CRISPR/Cas-based biosensors have developed as transformative tools for POC testing (POCT) because of their exceptional specificity and programmable cleavage activity. This review systematically evaluates HPV biomarkers, including DNA, RNA, and proteins, with a focus on CRISPR/Cas-enabled technologies for POC detection of HPV. We discuss the performance of diverse CRISPR/Cas systems for multiplex biomarker detection in POC settings for HPV infection screening. Recognizing the critical role of signal readout in POCT, we explore several signal-enhancement strategies, including nucleic acid amplification, preamplification-free assays, and integrated platforms tailored to POCT practicality, all aimed at balancing accuracy and practicality. Finally, we address key barriers to clinical translation and propose a roadmap that highlights the emerging role of AI-assisted platforms in advancing multiplexed detection, thereby supporting future decentralized HPV screening and contributing to the global elimination of cervical cancer.

abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)持续感染,特别是涉及高危亚型的感染,仍然是宫颈癌的主要驱动因素,突显了对快速、可及的点对点(POC)诊断方法的迫切需求。基于CRISPR/Cas的生物传感器因其卓越的特异性和可编程切割活性,已成为点对点检测(POCT)的变革性工具。本综述系统评估了HPV生物标志物,包括DNA、RNA和蛋白质,重点探讨了基于CRISPR/Cas技术的点对点HPV检测方法。我们讨论了多种CRISPR/Cas系统在点对点环境中用于多标志物检测的性能。认识到信号读取在POCT中的关键作用,我们探讨了多种信号增强策略,包括核酸扩增、无需预扩增的检测方法以及针对POCT实用性的集成平台,旨在平衡准确性和实用性。最后,我们讨论了临床转化的主要障碍,并提出了一条道路图,强调人工智能辅助平台在推进多标志物检测中的新兴作用,从而支持未来的去中心化HPV筛查,并有助于全球消除宫颈癌。

title: Knowledge gaps in human papillomavirus infection and vaccination among Polish medical students: an item-level cross-sectional analysis with an embedded feasibility evaluation of a multidisciplinary educational webinar
abstract: Abstract Background Poland introduced universal adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination only in June 2023, and coverage remains low. Because clinicians' recommendations strongly influence uptake, future physicians' preparedness matters. Polish studies report aggregate scores, which cannot show which facts are missing and so cannot guide curricular change. We mapped fourth-year medical students' baseline HPV knowledge at item level and assessed the feasibility of a multidisciplinary educational module. Methods In February 2024, within the Horizon 2020 project RIVER-EU, we conducted a cross-sectional knowledge assessment with an embedded single-arm pre–post feasibility component at the University of Zielona Góra, Poland. All 96 fourth-year students, none of whom had begun the infectious-diseases course, were invited to a voluntary five-hour expert-led webinar. A 20-item single-choice questionnaire was administered immediately before and after. The primary outcome was item difficulty; analyses comprised Wilson 95% confidence intervals, corrected item–total correlations, Kuder–Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) with KR-20-if-item-deleted, and McNemar's exact test with Bonferroni–Holm correction. Reporting follows TREND. Results Fifty-four of 96 invited students (56.2%) provided complete paired data: 37 women, 17 men. Mean baseline score was 13.19/20 (SD 3.76); KR-20 0.79. Performance varied more than fivefold across items (18.5–98.1%), so the mean concealed the educationally relevant pattern. Four items were answered correctly by half the cohort or fewer: cervical cancer as an uncommon individual outcome of infection (18.5%), the cervical cancer burden in Ukraine (20.4%), the vaccines' registered age (35.2%) and adult schedules (50.0%). All four discriminated acceptably (corrected item–total r 0.23–0.44), so none is an artifact of item construction. Natural history and epidemiology was the weakest domain (50.0%), virology and vaccine science the strongest (77.0%); sexes did not differ (p = 0.27). All 54 subsequently scored 20/20, but this ceiling, on an immediate unproctored post-test, is uninterpretable as learning. Conclusions Deficits concentrated in the applied and epidemiological content of HPV prevention - eligibility, age indications, dose schedules and individual cancer risk after infection not in the biology of the virus or its vaccines. The module was feasible to deliver and evaluate; controlled studies with proctored, delayed assessment are needed before claiming effectiveness.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒感染和疫苗接种在波兰医学学生中的知识空白:一项基于项目的横断面分析,嵌入式多学科教育网络研讨会的可行性评估
source_body_en: Abstract Background Poland introduced universal adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination only in June 2023, and coverage remains low. Because clinicians' recommendations strongly influence uptake, future physicians' preparedness matters. Polish studies report aggregate scores, which cannot show which facts are missing and so cannot guide curricular change. We mapped fourth-year medical students' baseline HPV knowledge at item level and assessed the feasibility of a multidisciplinary educational module. Methods In February 2024, within the Horizon 2020 project RIVER-EU, we conducted a cross-sectional knowledge assessment with an embedded single-arm pre–post feasibility component at the University of Zielona Góra, Poland. All 96 fourth-year students, none of whom had begun the infectious-diseases course, were invited to a voluntary five-hour expert-led webinar. A 20-item single-choice questionnaire was administered immediately before and after. The primary outcome was item difficulty; analyses comprised Wilson 95% confidence intervals, corrected item–total correlations, Kuder–Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) with KR-20-if-item-deleted, and McNemar's exact test with Bonferroni–Holm correction. Reporting follows TREND. Results Fifty-four of 96 invited students (56.2%) provided complete paired data: 37 women, 17 men. Mean baseline score was 13.19/20 (SD 3.76); KR-20 0.79. Performance varied more than fivefold across items (18.5–98.1%), so the mean concealed the educationally relevant pattern. Four items were answered correctly by half the cohort or fewer: cervical cancer as an uncommon individual outcome of infection (18.5%), the cervical cancer burden in Ukraine (20.4%), the vaccines' registered age (35.2%) and adult schedules (50.0%). All four discriminated acceptably (corrected item–total r 0.23–0.44), so none is an artifact of item construction. Natural history and epidemiology was the weakest domain (50.0%), virology and vaccine science the strongest (77.0%); sexes did not differ (p = 0.27). All 54 subsequently scored 20/20, but this ceiling, on an immediate unproctored post-test, is uninterpretable as learning. Conclusions Deficits concentrated in the applied and epidemiological content of HPV prevention - eligibility, age indications, dose schedules and individual cancer risk after infection not in the biology of the virus or its vaccines. The module was feasible to deliver and evaluate; controlled studies with proctored, delayed assessment are needed before claiming effectiveness.

title: Human Papillomavirus Testing Compared With Cytology for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Women Living With HIV in the Dominican Republic.
abstract: PURPOSE: Women living with HIV (WWH) face elevated cervical cancer risk, yet evidence supporting primary human papillomavirus (HPV) testing in low-resource settings remains limited. We compared HPV testing with cytology for detection of cervical precancer among WWH in the Dominican Republic to inform national screening strategies. METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis from US-Latin American-Caribbean HIV/HPV-Cancer Prevention Clinical Trials Network Trial 302 (Estudio Oportunidad, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05556772), 575 WWH contributed provider- and self-collected samples for cytology and HPV hierarchical testing. Women with positive results on cytology, provider-collected HPV testing, or self-collected HPV testing were referred for colposcopy and biopsy. Screening test characteristics were evaluated using centrally adjudicated histologic end points. RESULTS: Women with positive results on any screening test had higher HIV viral loads, lower CD4 counts, and were younger than women with screen-negative results. Sensitivity to detect cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3+) by cytology (66.7% [95% CI, 49.2 to 80.5]) was lower than sensitivity of provider-collected results with either 13 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes (93.9 [95% CI, 78.7 to 98.5]) or 8 hrHPV genotypes (84.8% [95% CI, 68.3 to 98.6]). Self-collected samples had the highest sensitivity (97.0%, 95% CI, 81.3 to 99.6). Cytology missed 33.3% of CIN3+, hrHPV testing of provider-collected samples missed 6.1%-15.2% of CIN3+, and hrHPV testing of self-collected samples missed 3.0% of CIN3+. CONCLUSION: Among WWH in the Dominican Republic, HPV testing, whether provider- or self-collected, outperformed cytology for detection of CIN3+. Both 13- and 8-genotype hrHPV panels demonstrated high sensitivity but low specificity, resulting in high referral rates to colposcopy. These findings support transitioning to primary HPV-based screening for WWH in the Dominican Republic to increase accuracy in detecting precancer and reduce the cervical cancer burden among WWH.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of HPV testing compared to cytology for detecting cervical precancer in women living with HIV (WWH) in the Dominican Republic. The research aimed to inform national screening strategies by comparing these methods in a cross-sectional analysis. The study included 575 WWH who provided provider- and self-collected samples for testing. Results showed that HPV testing, particularly with self-collected samples, had higher sensitivity for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3+) than cytology. The findings suggest that transitioning to primary HPV-based screening could improve detection accuracy and reduce cervical cancer burden among WWH. However, both 13- and 8-genotype HPV panels had high sensitivity but low specificity, leading to high referral rates for colposcopy. The study's evidence is strong, but limitations include the cross-sectional design and potential biases in sample collection and interpretation.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们比较了在多米尼加共和国的WWH中HPV检测与细胞学检查在宫颈癌前病变检测中的表现,以制定国家筛查策略。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究来自美国-拉丁美洲-加勒比海HIV/HPV-癌症预防临床试验网络第302项试验(Estudio Oportunidad,ClinicalTrials.gov编号:NCT05556772),共有575名WWH提供了由医护人员采集和自我采集的样本用于细胞学检查和HPV分层检测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 任何筛查检测结果为阳性的女性,其HIV病毒载量更高,CD4细胞计数更低,且年龄更小。

title: Study on the molecular mechanism of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition in HPV-associated cervical cancer through activation of miR-129.
abstract: BACKGROUND: HPV-associated cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women worldwide. The role of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and miR-129 in tumor progression remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To investigate miR-129 expression and its clinical significance in HPV-associated cervical cancer and to explore whether BMSCs regulate malignant phenotypes through miR-129. METHODS: miR-129 expression was measured by qRT-PCR in 77 cervical cancer and 30 normal cervical tissues. Associations with clinicopathological features and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Diagnostic value was assessed by ROC curve. Rat BMSCs were co-cultured with SiHa and HeLa cells. Following miR-129 overexpression or knockdown, cell proliferation (CCK-8, colony formation), invasion (Transwell) and expression of E-cadherin, N-cadherin and MRP1 (Western blot) were examined. RESULTS: miR-129 expression was significantly higher in cervical cancer tissues than in normal controls (3.24±0.56 vs. High miR-129 expression correlated with tumor size ≥3 cm (P=0.009), FIGO stage III-IV (P=0.0034) and lymph node metastasis (P=0.038). High expression was associated with shorter OS (median: 28.4 vs. 46.2 months; HR=2.944, 95%CI:1.484-5.842, P=0.002). The AUC was 0.788 (95%CI:0.693-0.884), with a cut-off of 1.85 (sensitivity:76.9%, specificity:70.4%). BMSC co-culture upregulated miR-129 expression (SiHa: 3.52±0.42 vs. miR-129 overexpression promoted proliferation, colony formation and invasion, while knockdown suppressed these phenotypes. Overexpression of miR-129 reduced E-cadherin (0.42±0.05 vs. 1.00±0.08, P<0.01) and increased N-cadherin (2.85±0.22 vs. 1.00±0.10, P<0.01) and MRP1 (2.46±0.18 vs. Knockdown of miR-129 partially reversed BMSC-induced changes in these proteins. CONCLUSION: miR-129 is significantly upregulated in HPV-associated cervical cancer and shows potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. BMSCs upregulate miR-129 in cervical cancer cells and miR-129 modulates proliferation, invasion, EMT marker expression and MRP1 expression. These findings suggest that the BMSCs/miR-129 axis may contribute to cervical cancer progression, but further in-vivo and mechanistic studies are needed.

source_body_en: BACKGROUND: HPV-associated cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women worldwide. The role of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and miR-129 in tumor progression remains unclear. Diagnostic value was assessed by ROC curve. Rat BMSCs were co-cultured with SiHa and HeLa cells. Following miR-129 overexpression or knockdown, cell proliferation (CCK-8, colony formation), invasion (Transwell) and expression of E-cadherin, N-cadherin and MRP1 (Western blot) were examined. RESULTS: miR-129 expression was significantly higher in cervical cancer tissues than in normal controls (3.24±0.56 vs. High miR-129 expression correlated with tumor size ≥3 cm (P=0.009), FIGO stage III-IV (P=0.0034) and lymph node metastasis (P=0.038). High expression was associated with shorter OS (median: 28.4 vs. 46.2 months; HR=2.944, 95%CI:1.484-5.842, P=0.002). The AUC was 0.788 (95%CI:0.693-0.884), with a cut-off of 1.85 (sensitivity:76.9%, specificity:70.4%). BMSC co-culture upregulated miR-129 expression (SiHa: 3.52±0.42 vs. miR-129 overexpression promoted proliferation, colony formation and invasion, while knockdown suppressed these phenotypes. Overexpression of miR-129 reduced E-cadherin (0.42±0.05 vs. 1.00±0.08, P<0.01) and increased N-cadherin (2.85±0.22 vs. 1.00±0.10, P<0.01) and MRP1 (2.46±0.18 vs. Knockdown of miR-129 partially reversed BMSC-induced changes in these proteins. CONCLUSION: miR-129 is significantly upregulated in HPV-associated cervical cancer and shows potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. BMSCs upregulate miR-129 in cervical cancer cells and miR-129 modulates proliferation, invasion, EMT marker expression and MRP1 expression. These findings suggest that the BMSCs/miR-129 axis may contribute to cervical cancer progression, but further in-vivo and mechanistic studies are needed.

title: Human Papillomavirus-Associated Papillomatous Lesions of the Oral Mucosa: A Narrative Review of Clinical, Histopathological, and Genotype-Specific Features
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes a spectrum of epithelial lesions, from transient infection and benign papillary proliferations to HPV-driven neoplasia. In the oral cavity, several papillomatous lesions share overlapping morphology but differ in genotype distribution and clinical significance. This narrative review synthesizes clinical, histopathological, and molecular evidence on these lesions and grades each primary study by the level of viral evidence it provides, from clinical diagnosis to transcriptionally active infection. HPV 6 and 11 predominate in HPV-positive condylomas and squamous papillomas and HPV 13 and 32 in multifocal epithelial hyperplasia, whereas the association of HPV 2 and 4 with oral verruca vulgaris rests on few studies; many squamous papillomas are HPV-negative. HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia, linked to transcriptionally active high-risk HPV, is a distinct potentially malignant entity whose frequency and transformation risk remain uncertain. Koilocytosis, papillary architecture, p16 expression, and HPV DNA detection do not by themselves establish causation, and evidence from oropharyngeal carcinoma cannot be extended to the oral cavity. We propose lesion-specific indications for supplementary HPV testing and summarize which conclusions are well supported and which remain uncertain.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with papillomatous lesions in the oral mucosa. It examines the clinical, histopathological, and genotype-specific features of these lesions, with an emphasis on HPV types and their role in disease progression. The central question is whether HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia represents a distinct potentially malignant entity and how different HPV genotypes contribute to various oral lesions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of clinical, histopathological, and molecular evidence. It grades each primary study based on the level of viral evidence it provides, ranging from clinical diagnosis to transcriptionally active infection. The review does not perform a meta-analysis but instead provides a qualitative summary of findings from the literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV 6 and 11 are predominantly associated with condylomas and squamous papillomas, while HPV 13 and 32 are linked to multifocal epithelial hyperplasia. However, the association of HPV 2 and 4 with oral verruca vulgaris is based on limited studies. Additionally, HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia is considered a distinct potentially malignant entity, though its frequency and transformation risk remain uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the use of markers such as koilocytosis, papillary architecture, p16 expression, and HPV DNA detection to establish causation. The review also highlights that evidence from oropharyngeal carcinoma cannot be directly extended to the oral cavity. Furthermore, the frequency and transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia are not well established, indicating a significant evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes lesion-specific indications for supplementary HPV testing and emphasizes the need to distinguish between well-supported conclusions and those that remain uncertain. It suggests that further research is required to clarify the role of specific HPV genotypes in oral lesions and to better understand the transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in oral papillomatous lesions, focusing on clinical, histopathological, and molecular features. It highlights the predominant association of HPV 6 and 11 with condylomas and squamous papillomas, while noting the limited evidence for HPV 2 and 4 in oral verruca vulgaris. The review identifies HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia as a potentially malignant entity, though its frequency and transformation risk are uncertain. It also cautions against using single markers like koilocytosis or p16 expression to establish causation and stresses the need for targeted HPV testing. The findings suggest that further research is necessary to clarify the pathogenic roles of specific HPV genotypes in oral lesions and to improve diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是临床、组织病理学和分子证据的叙述性综合。它根据每项研究提供的病毒证据水平对每个主要研究进行分级,从临床HPV到转录活性感染。本综述未进行荟萃分析,而是对文献中的发现进行了定性总结。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了针对不同病变的补充HPV检测指征,并强调了区分有充分支持的结论与仍不确定的结论的必要性。它建议需要进一步研究以明确特定HPV基因型在口腔病变中的作用,并更好地理解HPV相关口腔上皮异型增生的转化风险。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with papillomatous lesions in the oral mucosa. It examines the clinical, histopathological, and genotype-specific features of these lesions, with an emphasis on HPV types and their role in disease progression. The central question is whether HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia represents a distinct potentially malignant entity and how different HPV genotypes contribute to various oral lesions.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of clinical, histopathological, and molecular evidence. It grades each primary study based on the level of viral evidence it provides, ranging from clinical diagnosis to transcriptionally active infection. The review does not perform a meta-analysis but instead provides a qualitative summary of findings from the literature.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV 6 and 11 are predominantly associated with condylomas and squamous papillomas, while HPV 13 and 32 are linked to multifocal epithelial hyperplasia. However, the association of HPV 2 and 4 with oral verruca vulgaris is based on limited studies. Additionally, HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia is considered a distinct potentially malignant entity, though its frequency and transformation risk remain uncertain.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the use of markers such as koilocytosis, papillary architecture, p16 expression, and HPV DNA detection to establish causation. The review also highlights that evidence from oropharyngeal carcinoma cannot be directly extended to the oral cavity. Furthermore, the frequency and transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia are not well established, indicating a significant evidence gap.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes lesion-specific indications for supplementary HPV testing and emphasizes the need to distinguish between well-supported conclusions and those that remain uncertain. It suggests that further research is required to clarify the role of specific HPV genotypes in oral lesions and to better understand the transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关口腔黏膜乳头状病变:一种关于临床、组织病理学和基因型特异性特征的叙述性综述
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes a spectrum of epithelial lesions, from transient infection and benign papillary proliferations to HPV-driven neoplasia. In the oral cavity, several papillomatous lesions share overlapping morphology but differ in genotype distribution and clinical significance. This narrative review synthesizes clinical, histopathological, and molecular evidence on these lesions and grades each primary study by the level of viral evidence it provides, from clinical diagnosis to transcriptionally active infection. HPV 6 and 11 predominate in HPV-positive condylomas and squamous papillomas and HPV 13 and 32 in multifocal epithelial hyperplasia, whereas the association of HPV 2 and 4 with oral verruca vulgaris rests on few studies; many squamous papillomas are HPV-negative. HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia, linked to transcriptionally active high-risk HPV, is a distinct potentially malignant entity whose frequency and transformation risk remain uncertain. Koilocytosis, papillary architecture, p16 expression, and HPV DNA detection do not by themselves establish causation, and evidence from oropharyngeal carcinoma cannot be extended to the oral cavity. We propose lesion-specific indications for supplementary HPV testing and summarize which conclusions are well supported and which remain uncertain.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)可引起一系列上皮病变,从短暂感染和良性乳头状增生到由HPV驱动的肿瘤。在口腔内,几种乳头状病变在形态学上存在重叠,但其基因型分布和临床意义有所不同。本叙述性综述综合了这些病变的临床、组织病理学和分子证据,并根据每项研究提供的病毒证据水平对每个主要研究进行分级,从临床HPV到转录活性感染。HPV 6和11主要与HPV阳性尖锐湿疣和鳞状乳头状瘤相关,而HPV 13和32则与多灶性上皮增生相关;HPV 2和4与口腔寻常疣的关联基于少数研究;许多鳞状乳头状瘤为HPV阴性。与转录活性HPV相关的口腔上皮异型增生是一种独特的潜在恶性病变,其发生频率和转化风险仍不确定。koilocytosis、乳头状结构、p16表达和HPV DNA检测本身并不能确立因果关系,且口咽癌的证据不能直接推广到口腔。我们提出了针对不同病变的补充HPV检测指征,并总结了哪些结论有充分支持,哪些仍存在不确定性。
