title: The Neuroimmune Signature Underlying HPV Infection and Cervical Cancer Progression
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer, yet the multicellular signalling programmes that accompany disease progression remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated Single cell RNA sequencing, independent microarray and bulk RNA-sequencing meta analyses, and TCGA CESC tumor data to characterize the neuroimmune transcriptional architecture of HPV associated cervical disease. Single cell profiling revealed progressive remodeling of epithelial, stromal, endothelial and immune compartments across HPV infection, high grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and cervical cancer. Although immune dysregulation predominated, lesion and tumor states showed coordinated enrichment of nervous system associated programs, including synapse organization, trans-synaptic signaling, axon development, neurogenesis and neurotransmitter-related signaling. These programs formed interconnected networks with cytokine production, leukocyte activation, chemotaxis, cell adhesion, apoptosis, and immune effector regulation. Cross-platform integration identified a recurrent 12-gene neuroimmune signature associated with tumor grade related transcriptional variation, including CXCL12, P2RY6, P2RX5 and TACR1. Ligand receptor inference further highlighted glutamatergic, adrenergic, noradrenergic, GABAergic and purinergic signaling circuits. Notably, these signals were distributed across immune, epithelial, stromal and endothelial populations rather than confined to a canonical neural cell compartment. P2RX5 showed the strongest association with advanced tumor grade, whereas P2RY6, P2RY11 and GABRP displayed cell type and stage dependent regulation. Together, our findings define cervical carcinogenesis as a distributed neuroimmune state in which HPV associated immune evasion converges with ectopic neurotransmission-related programs, revealing candidate biomarkers and potentially actionable signaling axes in the cervical tumor microenvironment.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to understand the neuroimmune signaling programs associated with HPV infection and cervical cancer progression. The researchers integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, microarray, and bulk RNA-sequencing data from TCGA CESC tumor samples to characterize the neuroimmune transcriptional architecture of HPV-associated cervical disease. Their findings revealed progressive remodeling of multiple cellular compartments, including immune, epithelial, stromal, and endothelial, across different stages of HPV infection and cervical cancer. The study identified a 12-gene neuroimmune signature linked to tumor grade, highlighting key genes such as CXCL12, P2RY6, P2RX5, and TACR1. Additionally, ligand receptor inference uncovered various signaling circuits, including glutamatergic, adrenergic, noradrenergic, GABAergic, and purinergic, distributed across multiple cell types rather than confined to a canonical neural compartment. These results define cervical carcinogenesis as a distributed neuroimmune state, potentially offering new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. The study's evidence is strong, but its abstract-only nature limits the depth of analysis.

abstract_zh: 高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续感染是宫颈癌的主要病因,但伴随疾病进展的多细胞信号程序仍不完全明确。在这里,我们整合了单细胞RNA测序、独立的微阵列和批量RNA测序的元分析以及TCGA CESC肿瘤数据,以表征与HPV相关的宫颈疾病中的神经免疫转录架构。单细胞分析揭示了在HPV感染、高级别鳞状上皮内病变和宫颈癌过程中,上皮、基质、内皮和免疫组分的逐步重塑。尽管免疫失调占主导地位,但病变和肿瘤状态显示出与神经系统相关的程序的协调富集,包括突触组织、跨突触信号、轴突发育、神经发生和神经递质相关信号。这些程序与细胞因子产生、白细胞激活、趋化、细胞粘附、凋亡和免疫效应调节形成了相互连接的网络。跨平台整合识别出一个与肿瘤等级相关的12基因神经免疫特征,包括CXCL12、P2RY6、P2RX5和TACR1。配体受体推断进一步突出了谷氨酸能、肾上腺素能、去甲肾上腺素能、GABA能和嘌呤能信号通路。值得注意的是,这些信号分布在免疫、上皮、基质和内皮细胞群体中,而不是局限于经典的神经细胞组分。P2RX5与高级别肿瘤等级表现出最强的关联,而P2RY6、P2RY11和GABRP则表现出细胞类型和阶段依赖性的调控。综上所述,我们的研究结果定义了宫颈癌发生为一种分布式的神经免疫状态,在这种状态下,与HPV相关的免疫逃逸与异常神经递质传递相关程序汇聚,揭示了宫颈肿瘤微环境中潜在的生物标志物和可操作的信号轴。

title: Buschke-Löwenstein Tumor Spectrum Giant Condyloma with Mixed High- and Low-Risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Coinfection in an Adolescent with Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA): A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT), or giant condyloma acuminatum (GCA) is a rare, locally aggressive HPV-associated anogenital lesion characterized by extensive verrucous proliferation and a recognized potential for malignant transformation. Although BLT is classically linked to low-risk HPV genotypes 6 and 11, coexisting high-risk oncogenic genotypes may increase oncogenic potential, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. PURPOSE: To report a rare case of BLT-spectrum giant condyloma in an adolescent girl with autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) and mixed HPV 11, 16, and 18 coinfection, and to discuss the associated diagnostic challenges and potential oncogenic risk from a low resource setting perspective. CASE REPORT: A 16-year-old HIV-negative, unmarried adolescent presented with a progressively enlarging vulvar mass over 8 months, with marked growth over the preceding two months. Physical examination revealed a painful large verrucous condylomatous mass measuring 15 × 5 × 3 cm, covering the vaginal introitus. The lesion did not obstruct the urethral meatus. She also had severe AIHA requiring corticosteroid therapy and transfusion support. After multidisciplinary stabilization, excision and cauterization of vulvar, vaginal, and cervical lesions were performed, with the urethra protected intraoperatively using urinary catheter as a landmark. Histopathology showed papillomatous hyperplastic stratified squamous epithelium with marked acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, elongated rete ridges, and prominent koilocytotic changes, consistent with HPV-associated cytopathic effects, without stromal invasion or malignant transformation. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated increased Ki-67 proliferative activity, patchy (non-block) p16, and wild-type p53, consistent with a productive HPV-associated lesion without immunophenotypic evidence of transcriptionally active high-risk HPV or invasive carcinoma. HPV genotyping detected HPV 11, 16, and 18, whereas HPV 6 was negative. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of BLT-spectrum giant condyloma in adolescent with immune dysregulation. Despite benign histopathology, coexistence of high-risk HPV genotypes, rapid growth, and immunological impairment warrants cautious interpretation regarding potential premalignant risk and underscores the importance of adequate tissue sampling, long-term surveillance, and HPV prevention. These conclusions are based on a single case and should be interpreted accordingly.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: Buschke-Löwenstein肿瘤(BLT),或称为巨大型尖锐湿疣(GCA),是一种罕见的、局部侵袭性的与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的肛周生殖器病变,其特征为广泛的疣状增生,并具有已知的恶性转化潜力。本文旨在报告一例青少年女性患者合并自身免疫性溶血性贫血(AIHA)及混合型HPV 11、16和18感染的BLT谱系巨大型尖锐湿疣病例,并探讨其相关的诊断挑战及来自低资源环境视角的潜在致癌风险。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 病例报告:一名16岁、HIV阴性且未婚的青少年,近8个月来出现外阴肿块逐渐增大,最近两个月肿块显著增大。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 组织病理学显示乳头状增生性复层鳞状上皮,伴有显著的棘层增厚、角化过度、延长的乳头状沟和明显的空泡化细胞改变,与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关细胞病变效应一致,未见间质浸润或恶性转化。免疫组织化学检查显示Ki-67增殖活性增加,斑片状(非块状)p16表达,以及野生型p53,符合与HPV相关的活跃病变,无免疫表型证据显示高危型HPV转录活性或浸润性癌。HPV分型检测发现HPV 11、16和18型,而HPV 6型为阴性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些结论基于单一病例,应据此进行解释。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 尽管组织病理学表现良性,但高危型HPV基因型共存、快速增殖以及免疫学损害提示需要谨慎解读潜在的癌前风险,并强调了充分的组织取样、长期监测监测以及HPV预防的重要性。

title_zh: Buschke-Löwenstein肿瘤谱系:一名青少年自身免疫性溶血性贫血(AIHA)患者合并高危型HPV与低危型HPV混合感染的巨大型尖锐湿疣:一例病例报告
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT), or giant condyloma acuminatum (GCA) is a rare, locally aggressive HPV-associated anogenital lesion characterized by extensive verrucous proliferation and a recognized potential for malignant transformation. Although BLT is classically linked to low-risk HPV genotypes 6 and 11, coexisting high-risk oncogenic genotypes may increase oncogenic potential, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. PURPOSE: To report a rare case of BLT-spectrum giant condyloma in an adolescent girl with autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) and mixed HPV 11, 16, and 18 coinfection, and to discuss the associated diagnostic challenges and potential oncogenic risk from a low resource setting perspective. CASE REPORT: A 16-year-old HIV-negative, unmarried adolescent presented with a progressively enlarging vulvar mass over 8 months, with marked growth over the preceding two months. Physical examination revealed a painful large verrucous condylomatous mass measuring 15 × 5 × 3 cm, covering the vaginal introitus. The lesion did not obstruct the urethral meatus. She also had severe AIHA requiring corticosteroid therapy and transfusion support. After multidisciplinary stabilization, excision and cauterization of vulvar, vaginal, and cervical lesions were performed, with the urethra protected intraoperatively using urinary catheter as a landmark. Histopathology showed papillomatous hyperplastic stratified squamous epithelium with marked acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, elongated rete ridges, and prominent koilocytotic changes, consistent with HPV-associated cytopathic effects, without stromal invasion or malignant transformation. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated increased Ki-67 proliferative activity, patchy (non-block) p16, and wild-type p53, consistent with a productive HPV-associated lesion without immunophenotypic evidence of transcriptionally active high-risk HPV or invasive carcinoma. HPV genotyping detected HPV 11, 16, and 18, whereas HPV 6 was negative. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of BLT-spectrum giant condyloma in adolescent with immune dysregulation. Despite benign histopathology, coexistence of high-risk HPV genotypes, rapid growth, and immunological impairment warrants cautious interpretation regarding potential premalignant risk and underscores the importance of adequate tissue sampling, long-term surveillance, and HPV prevention. These conclusions are based on a single case and should be interpreted accordingly.
abstract_zh: 背景:Buschke-Löwenstein肿瘤(BLT),或称为巨大型尖锐湿疣(GCA),是一种罕见的、局部侵袭性的与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的泌尿生殖器病变,其特征是广泛的疣状增生,并具有已知的恶性转化潜力。尽管BLT传统上与低危型HPV基因型6和11相关,但同时存在的高危型致癌基因型可能会增加致癌潜力,尤其是在免疫功能低下的个体中。目的:报告一例罕见的BLT谱系巨大型尖锐湿疣病例,该病例发生于一名患有自身免疫性溶血性贫血(AIHA)的青少年女孩,并伴有混合型HPV 11、16和18感染,讨论其相关的诊断挑战及从低资源环境视角出发的潜在致癌风险。病例报告:一名16岁的HIV阴性、未婚青少年,因8个月内逐渐增大的外阴肿块就诊,其中最近两个月增长显著。体格检查发现一个疼痛明显的大型疣状尖锐湿疣样肿块,大小为15 × 5 × 3 cm,覆盖阴道口。该病变未阻塞尿道口。她还伴有严重的AIHA,需要糖皮质激素治疗和输血支持。在多学科团队稳定病情后,进行了外阴、阴道和宫颈病变的切除和烧灼术,并在手术过程中使用尿管作为标志物以保护尿道。组织病理学显示乳头状增生的复层鳞状上皮,伴有显著的棘层增厚、过度角化、延长的乳头状突起以及明显的空泡样细胞变化,符合HPV相关的细胞病变效应,未见间质浸润或恶性转化。免疫组织化学检查显示Ki-67增殖活性增加,p16呈斑片状(非块状)表达,p53呈野生型,符合与HPV相关的活跃病变,但未见免疫表型证据显示转录活性高危型HPV或浸润性癌。HPV基因分型检测发现HPV 11、16和18,而HPV 6为阴性。结论:该病例展示了在免疫调节异常的青少年中,BLT谱系巨大型尖锐湿疣的诊断复杂性。尽管组织病理学结果为良性,但同时存在高危型HPV基因型、快速生长以及免疫功能损害,提示需要谨慎评估潜在的癌前病变风险,并强调了充分的组织取样、长期监测以及HPV预防的重要性。这些结论基于单一病例,应据此进行解读。

title: Multiple Extraintestinal Malignancies and HPV16-Associated Neoplasms in Crohn’s Disease Under Prolonged Immunosuppression: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Crohn’s disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the gastrointestinal tract with an increased risk for malignancy, particularly in patients undergoing immunosuppressive therapy. Case Presentation: This report describes the 23-year clinical course of a 20-year-old woman diagnosed with CD who, under prolonged therapy with azathioprine (AZA), developed three distinct carcinomas. The patient sequentially developed low-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 1; Year 10; 3 years of AZA), a conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma (Year 14; 7 years of AZA; followed by a 10-month AZA pause), and a cutaneous basal cell carcinoma (Year 17; ~9.2 cumulative years of AZA). After CD recurrence and AZA resumption, CIN 2 was detected (Year 18; ~10.2 cumulative years of AZA). In the 18th year, AZA therapy was discontinued. Within less than one year (Year 19), cervical squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed. In Year 23, CD was controlled, without neoplasms documented. High-risk HPV16 DNA was detected in cervical and conjunctival malignancies by PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Immunohistochemical analysis showed high Ki-67 and p16 expression and CD4+ cell predominance, supporting an association of HPV16 in these neoplasms. The short interval between CIN 2 and invasive CSCC detection is unusual. While this coincided with chronic immunosuppression, direct causality currently cannot be inferred; however, the patient’s chronic immune dysregulation and immunosuppression may be contributing factors. Conclusions: This case highlights the temporal co-occurrence of Crohn’s disease, prolonged immunosuppression, and HPV16 infection. These findings raise the need for vigilant extraintestinal cancer surveillance, regular screening, and HPV vaccination during chronic immunosuppression.
authors: Neuzenir da Silva de Abreu Oliveira

abstract_zh: 背景:克罗恩病(CD)是一种胃肠道慢性炎症性疾病,其恶性肿瘤风险增加,尤其是在接受免疫抑制治疗的患者中。病例报告:本文描述了一位20岁女性患者被诊断为CD后,在长期使用硫唑嘌呤(AZA)治疗期间,先后发展出三种不同的癌变。该患者在使用AZA治疗3年后出现低级别宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN 1;第10年),在治疗7年后(第14年)停用AZA 10个月后出现结膜鳞状细胞癌,以及在约9.2年累计AZA治疗后(第17年)出现皮肤基底细胞癌。在第18年,CD复发并重新开始AZA治疗,此时检测到CIN 2(约10.2年累计AZA治疗)。在第18年,AZA治疗被终止。不到一年(第19年),诊断出宫颈鳞状细胞癌。第23年时,CD得到控制,未见肿瘤记录。通过PCR检测到宫颈和结膜恶性肿瘤中存在高危型HPV16 DNA,并通过桑格测序确认。免疫组化分析显示高Ki-67和p16表达以及CD4+细胞占优,支持这些肿瘤与HPV16的关联。CIN 2与侵袭性宫颈鳞状细胞癌(CSCC)之间的时间间隔较短,这在临床上较为罕见。虽然这一时间点与慢性免疫抑制治疗重合,但目前尚无法直接推断因果关系;然而,患者的慢性免疫失调和免疫抑制可能为这些肿瘤的形成提供了贡献因素。结论:该病例突显了克罗恩病、长期免疫抑制治疗和HPV16感染在时间上的共存。这些发现强调了在慢性免疫抑制治疗期间对肠外癌症进行警惕性监测、定期筛查以及HPV 疫苗接种的重要性。局限性与证据强度:CIN 2与侵袭性CSCC之间的时间间隔较短,这在临床上较为罕见。虽然这一时间点与慢性免疫抑制治疗重合,但目前尚无法直接推断因果关系;然而,患者的慢性免疫失调和免疫抑制可能为这些肿瘤的形成提供了贡献因素。

title: Comparative Evaluation of E6/E7 mRNA Expression and Viral DNA Load in Cervical Lesions With Multiple High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are frequently detected in cervical screening, but their biological interactions and clinical significance remain unclear. Because HPV DNA detection indicates viral presence but not transcriptional activity, this exploratory study evaluated viral load, genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression, localization, and follow-up. METHODS: Among 12 000 cervical specimens tested for hrHPV, 598 were positive and 72 showed multiple genotypes. Viral load was assessed using the BioPerfectus Multiplex Real-Time assay. A tissue-available subset of 36 dual HPV16 + 52 or HPV16 + 58 cases was analyzed by duplex RNAscope for genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression and localization. Diagnoses were categorized as benign, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Viral load and RNAscope analyses used incompletely matched subsets and were interpreted as complementary, not paired. RESULTS: Elevated viral load (≥4.00 log10 copies/10 000 cells) was associated with HSIL. In cohort-level analyses, diffuse (+++) E6/E7 mRNA expression was more frequent in HSIL than elevated viral load (95.2% vs 55.5%, P = .01). RNAscope-negative cases were mostly benign or LSIL and showed no progression. Genotype-specific signals were spatially distinct, with rare overlap. Dual-positive cells showed fewer RNA signals than adjacent single-positive cells (P < .001). Higher E6/E7 mRNA expression showed possible association with LSIL progression, but events were limited. CONCLUSIONS: In multiplex hrHPV infection, transcriptional activity may better reflect cervical lesion biology than viral DNA burden alone. Genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression may complement HPV DNA load. Spatially distinct signals and reduced signal intensity in rare dual-positive cells suggest possible interactions between coinfecting hrHPV genotypes, but require prospective validation in fully matched cohorts.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between E6/E7 mRNA expression and viral DNA load in cervical lesions with multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections. It analyzed 12,000 cervical specimens, identifying 598 hrHPV-positive cases and 72 with multiple genotypes. A subset of 36 dual HPV16 + 52 or HPV16 + 58 cases was examined using duplex RNAscope to assess mRNA expression and localization. Results showed that elevated viral load was associated with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), while diffuse E6/E7 mRNA expression was more frequent in HSIL than in elevated viral load. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在宫颈筛查中,多重高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)感染经常被检测到,但其生物学相互作用和临床意义仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在12 000份用于hrHPV检测的宫颈标本中,有598份呈阳性,其中72份显示多重基因型。选取36份双阳性HPV16 + 52或HPV16 + 58的组织可用子集,通过双色RNAscope技术分析基因型特异性E6/E7 mRNA表达和定位。
elements_zh.methods: 使用BioPerfectus Multiplex Real-Time检测方法评估病毒载量。诊断分为良性、低级别鳞状上皮内病变(LSIL)或高级别鳞状上皮内病变(HSIL)。病毒载量和RNAscope分析使用不完全匹配的子集,并被解释为互补而非配对分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 病毒载量升高(≥4.00 log10 copies/10 000 cells)与HSIL相关。在基因型水平分析中,弥漫性(+++) E6/E7 mRNA表达在HSIL中的发生率高于病毒载量升高(95.2% vs 55.5%,P = .01)。RNAscope阴性病例多为良性或LSIL,且无进展。基因型特异性信号在空间上相互分离,重叠较少。双阳性细胞的RNA信号比相邻单阳性细胞更少(P < .001)。更高的E6/E7 mRNA表达可能与LSIL进展有关,但事件有限。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在多重hrHPV感染中,转录活性可能比单独的病毒DNA负担更能反映宫颈病变的生物学特性。基因型特异性E6/E7 mRNA表达可能补充HPV DNA载量。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,E6/E7 mRNA表达可能为多重hrHPV感染相关宫颈病变进展提供额外的见解,可能有助于改善诊断和预后方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于病毒载量和RNAscope分析使用了不完全匹配的子集,这可能限制了所观察到的关联强度。由于研究的探索性质和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 背景:在宫颈筛查中,多重高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)感染经常被检测到,但其生物学相互作用和临床意义仍不清楚。由于HPV DNA检测仅表明病毒存在而非转录活性,本探索性研究评估了病毒载量、基因型特异性E6/E7 mRNA表达、定位及随访情况。方法:在12 000份用于hrHPV检测的宫颈标本中,有598份呈阳性,其中72份显示多重基因型。使用BioPerfectus Multiplex Real-Time检测方法评估病毒载量。选取36份双阳性HPV16 + 52或HPV16 + 58的组织可用子集,通过双色RNAscope技术分析基因型特异性E6/E7 mRNA表达和定位。诊断分为良性、低级别鳞状上皮内病变(LSIL)或高级别鳞状上皮内病变(HSIL)。病毒载量和RNAscope分析使用不完全匹配的子集,并被解释为互补而非配对分析。结果:病毒载量升高(≥4.00 log10 copies/10 000 cells)与HSIL相关。在基因型水平分析中,弥漫性(+++) E6/E7 mRNA表达在HSIL中的发生率高于病毒载量升高(95.2% vs 55.5%,P = .01)。RNAscope阴性病例多为良性或LSIL,且无进展。基因型特异性信号在空间上相互分离,重叠较少。双阳性细胞的RNA信号比相邻单阳性细胞更少(P < .001)。更高的E6/E7 mRNA表达可能与LSIL进展有关,但事件有限。结论:在多重hrHPV感染中,转录活性可能比单独的病毒DNA负担更能反映宫颈病变的生物学特性。基因型特异性E6/E7 mRNA表达可能补充HPV DNA载量。空间上分离的信号和双阳性细胞中信号强度的降低提示可能有感染hrHPV基因型之间的相互作用,但需要在完全匹配的基因型中进行前瞻性验证。

title: High-risk HPV integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors
abstract: Background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.We aimed to characterize the regulatory architecture associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate its functional relevance in preclinical models.Methods: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int ) were established.Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.Results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo.Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs).Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.Spatial and single-cell multi-omic analyses further confirmed that HSTF activation was triggered by hrHPV integration, which could be blocked by HSTF inhibition in vivo.Conclusions: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPVdriven carcinogenesis.Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory program may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int) were established to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.
analysis.methods: Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to evaluate the regulatory changes associated with hrHPV integration.
analysis.main_results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo. Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs). Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPV-driven carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory programs may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on preclinical models and does not include human clinical trials, which limits the direct applicability of findings to human populations. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on in vitro and in vivo models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs). The research aimed to characterize the regulatory changes associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate their functional relevance in preclinical models. Using a combination of viral integration mapping, chromatin profiling, transcriptomics, and spatial analyses, the study found that hrHPV integration hotspots are enriched for HSTF motifs, which correlate with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, and enhanced transcriptional activity in cancer progression. These results suggest that HSTFs play a critical role in HPV-driven carcinogenesis and that targeting their regulatory programs could offer new therapeutic strategies for hrHPV-related cancers. However, the study's reliance on preclinical models limits the direct translation of findings to human populations, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

abstract_zh: 背景:高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)DNA整合到宿主 基因组中会促进hrHPV相关癌变中的持续病毒感染和恶性进展,但与整合相关的顺式调控程序仍不完全明确,限制了潜在治疗脆弱性的识别。我们旨在表征与hrHPV整合相关的调控架构,并评估其在临床前模型中的功能相关性。方法:建立了携带整合HPV16上游调控区-E6/E7序列的人类宫颈上皮类器官和一个HPV16整合的小鼠模型(14 E2.2 HPV16-int)。通过整合病毒整合图谱、基序富集分析、染色质可及性与组蛋白修饰分析、三维染色质相互作用分析、批量和单细胞转录组学、空间转录组学以及患者来源的类器官/异种移植模型,评估与hrHPV整合相关的调控变化和药物干预。结果:携带hrHPV整合的人类上皮类器官和小鼠在体外和体内均重现了逐渐恶化的恶性表型。在宫颈癌和头颈癌数据集中,hrHPV整合热点富含一组定义的25种HPV特异性条带转录因子(HSTFs)的基序。在hrHPV阳性上皮癌轨迹中,HSTF基序密度越高,染色质可及性、活跃的组蛋白标记、超级增强子-启动子相互作用以及HSTF调控活性均相应增强。空间和单细胞多组学分析进一步证实,HSTF的激活是由hrHPV整合触发的,这种激活可以在体内通过HSTF抑制被阻断。结论:这些发现揭示了与hrHPV整合相关的顺式调控网络,该网络促进染色质重塑和转录激活,从而推动HPV驱动的癌变。针对HSTF相关的调控程序可能代表一种治疗高危型HPV整合的癌前病变和癌症的有前景的策略。

title: Presence of HPV infection, not age, identifies vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a 847-patient multivariable analysis with 40- and 45-year age-cutoff sensitivity testing
abstract: Background Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is a precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with two biologically distinct pathways: HPV-associated and HPV-independent disease. Whether chronological age is independently associated with VIN after adjusting for HPV infection and multifocal lower genital tract disease remains unclear. Methods ​We analyzed 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls. Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed. A further sensitivity analysis was restricted to high-grade lesions (HSIL/VIN2–3 vs. Results Univariable analysis showed that VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs). At the 45-year cutoff, concurrent CIN was more frequent in the older group (12.2% vs. In the HSIL-only sensitivity analysis, continuous age remained non-significant (P = 0.492), while HPV infection was a strong independent risk factor (P 0.05). HPV infection was consistently and independently associated with VIN across all models (overall adjusted OR 3.146, P < 0.001; stratified aOR 2.812–3.859, all P < 0.001). Conclusions The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age. Vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.

It analyzed 847 women, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls, using univariable comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and sensitivity analyses with age cutoffs. The results showed VIN patients were younger and had a higher HPV infection rate compared to non-VIN controls. The marginal significance of age was attributed to residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease. The study concluded that VIN should be identified by HPV infection status rather than age, emphasizing the need for HPV-focused screening. The findings have implications for clinical practice, suggesting that vulvar inspections should prioritize HPV testing and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia detection over age-based criteria. The evidence is strong, but the study's design may limit its ability to fully control for confounding factors.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定HPV感染或年龄与外阴上皮内瘤变(VIN)之间的关联强度,因为VIN是外阴鳞状细胞癌的前驱病变,具有两种生物学上不同的发病途径:HPV相关和HPV无关的疾病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2022年4月至2025年12月期间因阴道镜检查和外阴评估而就诊的847名女性中进行了多变量分析,其中包括568名VIN患者和279名非VIN对照组。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了单变量比较、按年龄分层的多变量逻辑回归分析(Enter方法;完整病例数n = 673)以及使用40岁和45岁分界点的敏感性分析,以评估年龄、HPV感染与VIN之间的关联。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在主要模型中连续年龄的边缘统计学显著性反映了HPV感染和多灶性疾病积累的残留混杂因素,而非年龄本身的独立致病作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,外阴检查应依据HPV感染状态和并发的下生殖道肿瘤,而非随意的年龄分界点,特别是考虑到无症状VIN的高患病率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究设计包括单变量比较和多变量逻辑回归分析,可能在控制所有混杂因素方面存在局限,但鉴于HPV感染在所有模型中均一致且独立地与VIN相关,证据是强有力的。

title: Enhancing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Communication with Mobile Health: Usability Insights from Caregivers and Health Care Providers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in preventing cancer, uptake remains suboptimal, especially among rural and underserved populations. Digital communication tools such as mobile health (mHealth) applications have the potential to improve access to accurate vaccine information and support shared decision-making. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the usability, acceptability, and perceived usefulness of a newly developed mHealth app for HPV vaccine communication in comparison to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) HPV vaccine Web site. METHODS: Using a mixed-methods design and guided by the Health Belief Model and the mHealth Agile Development and Evaluation Lifecycle, caregivers, and health care providers were randomized to explore both the CDC Web site and the mHealth app in alternating order. Participants were asked to complete a session answering HPV vaccine questions with each tool and completed the mHealth App Usability Questionnaire, Propensity to Trust, and NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) after each session. Qualitative questions were asked after each session to capture additional feedback on items such as navigation and readability. Transcripts were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Quantitative results showed no difference between the tools in terms of being easy to use, requiring similar amounts of effort, and trust in the tool. Qualitative themes revealed that participants appreciated the app's streamlined navigation, tailored content, and readability. In contrast, the CDC Web site was seen as credible but often difficult to navigate, especially when searching for nuanced or specific vaccine information. CONCLUSION: Tailored mHealth tools developed with user-centered design principles may better meet the informational and usability needs of caregivers and health care providers compared with existing web-based resources. These findings support further development and integration of mHealth tools into vaccine communication strategies to enhance HPV vaccine communication.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the usability, acceptability, and perceived usefulness of a newly developed mHealth app for HPV vaccine communication in comparison to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) HPV vaccine Web site. METHODS: Using a mixed-methods design and guided by the Health Belief Model and the mHealth Agile Development and Evaluation Lifecycle, caregivers, and health care providers were randomized to explore both the CDC Web site and the mHealth app in alternating order. Participants were asked to complete a session answering HPV vaccine questions with each tool and completed the mHealth App Usability Questionnaire, Propensity to Trust, and NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) after each session. Qualitative questions were asked after each session to capture additional feedback on items such as navigation and readability. Transcripts were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Quantitative results showed no difference between the tools in terms of being easy to use, requiring similar amounts of effort, and trust in the tool. Qualitative themes revealed that participants appreciated the app's streamlined navigation, tailored content, and readability. In contrast, the CDC Web site was seen as credible but often difficult to navigate, especially when searching for nuanced or specific vaccine information. CONCLUSION: Tailored mHealth tools developed with user-centered design principles may better meet the informational and usability needs of caregivers and health care providers compared with existing web-based resources. These findings support further development and integration of mHealth tools into vaccine communication strategies to enhance HPV vaccine communication.
title_original: Enhancing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Communication with Mobile Health: Usability Insights from Caregivers and Health Care Providers.

abstract_zh: 背景:尽管人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗在预防癌症方面有效,但其接种率仍不理想,尤其是在农村和医疗资源不足的人群中。数字通信工具如移动健康(mHealth)应用程序有潜力改善获取准确疫苗信息的途径,并支持共同决策。研究目的:本研究旨在评估一种新开发的mHealth应用程序在与美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)的HPV 疫苗网站进行比较时的可用性、可接受性和感知有用性。研究方法:采用混合方法设计,依据健康信念模型和mHealth敏捷开发与评估生命周期,护理人员和医疗保健提供者被随机分配以交替顺序探索CDC网站和mHealth应用程序。参与者在使用每种工具回答HPV 疫苗相关问题后,完成了mHealth应用程序可用性问卷、信任倾向量表和NASA任务负荷指数(NASA-TLX)。在每次会话后,还通过定性问题收集关于导航和可读性的额外反馈。转录文本采用归纳主题分析法进行分析。研究结果:定量结果显示,两种工具在易用性、所需努力程度以及对工具的信任度方面没有显著差异。定性主题分析表明,参与者赞赏应用程序的简洁导航、定制内容和良好的可读性。相比之下,CDC网站被认为具有可信度,但在寻找细致或特定的疫苗信息时往往难以导航。研究结论:与现有的基于网络的资源相比,采用以用户为中心设计原则开发的定制mHealth工具可能更能满足护理人员和医疗保健提供者的信息和可用性需求。这些发现支持进一步开发和整合mHealth工具到疫苗沟通策略中,以增强HPV 疫苗的沟通效果。

title: Presence of Human Papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr Virus in Breast Cancer Biopsies as Potential Risk Factors
abstract: Introduction: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population.Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.Objective: To detect the presence of human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus in breast cancer biopsies in order to establish a possible link between infection with these viral agents and the development of this pathology.Methods: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).Results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.Conclusion: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer; however, studies allowing for the role of these viruses in the development of the disease to be elucidated are required.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in breast cancer biopsies to determine their potential role as risk factors. The research is motivated by the fact that breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Venezuelan women, and previous associations between HPV and EBV and breast cancer have been noted. The study collected fresh biopsies from patients with breast cancer and those with benign pathology at the Hospital Universitario de Caracas. HPV was detected using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit, while EBV was identified with the Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit. Results showed that 63.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for HPV DNA, and 13.6% for EBV DNA, compared to 4.5% for each virus in benign samples. Additionally, 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infections with low and high oncogenic risk HPV genotypes. The authors suggest that HPV and EBV may be important risk factors for breast cancer, though further studies are needed to clarify their role. The study's findings are limited by the lack of detailed limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: Post-Treatment Surveillance After Conisation for CIN2/3 in Norway: Long-Term CIN3+ Risk Stratification Comparing HPV DNA Testing with Cytology/HPV16/18/45 mRNA Co-Testing
abstract: We compared surveillance strategies in a retrospective regional cohort of 2136 women who underwent conisation for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2/3) in 2016–2020. Using results from the first eligible visit 90–548 days after treatment, we evaluated cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 messenger RNA (mRNA) testing, individually and in combination. We also evaluated an exploratory referral strategy adapted from the Addressing the Need for Advanced HPV Diagnostics (ATHENA) study. Histological outcomes were ascertained through 2025. Median available administrative follow-up was 7.24 years. CIN3+ (CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ or invasive cervical cancer) was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). For CIN3+, HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity and 24.4% positivity. Adding mRNA positivity to high-grade+ cytology increased CIN3+ sensitivity from 60.8% to 82.4%, with 92.1% specificity and 10.4% test positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%), with 73.5% specificity. The ATHENA-derived strategy achieved 90.5% sensitivity and 83.1% specificity, with 19.4% classified as referral-positive. Among women with equivocal or low-grade cytology, CIN3+ was recorded in 18.6% with positive mRNA and 2.5% with negative mRNA. Cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation. Prospective evaluation is needed to establish safe surveillance intervals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different post-treatment surveillance strategies for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3 (CIN2/3) in identifying long-term CIN3+ risk, addressing the need for improved risk stratification methods after conisation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective regional cohort of 2136 women who underwent conisation for CIN2/3 between 2016 and 2020 was studied. Histological outcomes were ascertained through 2025, with median administrative follow-up of 7.24 years.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated cytology, HPV DNA testing, and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 mRNA co-testing, individually and in combination, using results from the first eligible visit 90–548 days after treatment. An exploratory referral strategy adapted from the ATHENA study was also assessed.
analysis.main_results: CIN3+ was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity, and 24.4% positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%) with 73.5% specificity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation, offering a more sensitive approach for detecting CIN3+.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of more effective surveillance strategies for cervical cancer risk after treatment, potentially improving long-term monitoring and reducing the risk of missed diagnoses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and lacks prospective evaluation, which limits confidence in the proposed surveillance intervals. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated post-treatment surveillance strategies for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3 (CIN2/3) in a regional cohort of 2136 women in Norway. The primary aim was to assess the effectiveness of HPV DNA testing, cytology, and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 mRNA co-testing in identifying long-term CIN3+ risk. Results showed that HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity and 78.0% specificity, while combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed sensitivity (95.9%) with 73.5% specificity. The authors suggest that cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support improved risk stratification after conisation. However, the study is retrospective and lacks prospective evaluation, which limits confidence in the proposed surveillance intervals. The findings may inform more effective long-term monitoring strategies for cervical cancer risk post-treatment.

elements_en.main_results: CIN3+ was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity, and 24.4% positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%) with 73.5% specificity.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation, offering a more sensitive approach for detecting CIN3+.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of more effective surveillance strategies for cervical cancer risk after treatment, potentially improving long-term monitoring and reducing the risk of missed diagnoses.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and lacks prospective evaluation, which limits confidence in the proposed surveillance intervals. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for bias.

title_zh: 挪威宫颈上皮内瘤变2/3级(CIN2/3)锥切术后CIN3+长期风险分层:比较人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测与细胞学/HPV16/18/45 mRNA联合检测策略
source_body_en: We compared surveillance strategies in a retrospective regional cohort of 2136 women who underwent conisation for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2/3) in 2016–2020. Using results from the first eligible visit 90–548 days after treatment, we evaluated cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 messenger RNA (mRNA) testing, individually and in combination. We also evaluated an exploratory referral strategy adapted from the Addressing the Need for Advanced HPV Diagnostics (ATHENA) study. Histological outcomes were ascertained through 2025. Median available administrative follow-up was 7.24 years. CIN3+ (CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ or invasive cervical cancer) was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). For CIN3+, HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity and 24.4% positivity. Adding mRNA positivity to high-grade+ cytology increased CIN3+ sensitivity from 60.8% to 82.4%, with 92.1% specificity and 10.4% test positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%), with 73.5% specificity. The ATHENA-derived strategy achieved 90.5% sensitivity and 83.1% specificity, with 19.4% classified as referral-positive. Among women with equivocal or low-grade cytology, CIN3+ was recorded in 18.6% with positive mRNA and 2.5% with negative mRNA. Cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation. Prospective evaluation is needed to establish safe surveillance intervals.
abstract_zh: 我们对2016年至2020年间接受锥切术治疗宫颈上皮内瘤变2/3级(CIN2/3)的2136名女性进行了回顾性区域研究,比较了锥切术后不同检测策略。利用锥切术后90至548天内首次符合资格的访问结果,我们评估了细胞学检测、人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测以及HPV16/18/45 E6/E7信使RNA(mRNA)检测,分别单独使用和联合使用。我们还评估了一种探索性转诊策略,该策略借鉴了《应对高级HPV诊断需求》(ATHENA)研究。组织学结果通过2025年确认,中位数行政随访时间为7.24年。CIN3+(CIN3、原位腺癌或侵袭性宫颈癌)在74名女性中被记录(3.5%)。对于CIN3+,HPV DNA检测的敏感性为93.2%,特异性为78.0%,阳性率为24.4%。将mRNA阳性结果与高级别+细胞学结果结合,CIN3+的敏感性从60.8%提高到82.4%,特异性为92.1%,阳性率为10.4%。将ASC-US+细胞学结果与mRNA阳性结果结合,达到了最高的观察到的CIN3+敏感性(95.9%),特异性为73.5%。基于ATHENA研究的策略实现了90.5%的敏感性和83.1%的特异性,其中19.4%被归类为转诊阳性。在细胞学结果为可疑或低级别的情况下,mRNA阳性者中有18.6%被记录为CIN3+,而mRNA阴性者中仅2.5%被记录为CIN3+。细胞学和基因型特异性mRNA联合检测可能有助于锥切术后风险分层。需要前瞻性评估以确定安全的锥切术后随访间隔。

title: Factors associated with biopsy-confirmed high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) in women undergoing colposcopy: role of HPV infection, vaccination status, and cytology
abstract: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. HPV infection, cytological abnormalities, and HPV vaccination status may be associated with CIN2+. This study evaluated factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2 + in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 246 women undergoing colposcopy, from January 2014 to January 2024 were included. HPV was detected using the PaxView ® Kit. CIN2 + was defined as histopathologically confirmed CIN2, CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ, or invasive cervical cancer. HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+. adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Results Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. HPV status and cytological findings differed significantly between women with CIN2 + and CIN2− (both p < 0.001). HPV16/18 was more frequent among women with CIN2 + than CIN2− (56.0% vs. 28.6%), whereas HPV-negative results were less frequent (18.0% vs. Similarly, HSIL cytology (38.0% vs. 10.7%) and lack of HPV vaccination (42.0% vs. 16.8%) were more common in the CIN2 + group. In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+. Age, marital status and other high-risk HPV genotypes were not significantly associated with CIN2+. Conclusion In this Iranian colposcopy population, HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology were independently associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+. Lack of HPV vaccination was also associated with higher odds of CIN2+, but this finding should be interpreted cautiously, as the timing of vaccination relative to HPV exposure was not recorded and the association may reflect unmeasured confounding parameters. Prospective studies focusing on vaccination timing and pre-vaccination HPV status are needed to clarify this association.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. This study aimed to evaluate factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 246 women undergoing colposcopy from January 2014 to January 2024. The study focused on women with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ and compared them with those without such lesions.
analysis.methods: HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+.
analysis.main_results: Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology are important factors in the development of CIN2+. This information can inform cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies, particularly in populations where HPV vaccination rates are low.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated factors associated with biopsy-confirmed high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) in women undergoing colposcopy, focusing on HPV infection, vaccination status, and cytology. A retrospective cross-sectional design was used, including 246 women from 2014 to 2024. HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression. Among the participants, 20.3% had CIN2+, with HPV16/18 infection, lack of HPV vaccination, and HSIL cytology independently associated with CIN2+. The study highlights the importance of HPV16/18 and HSIL in CIN2+ development, but the association with vaccination status requires cautious interpretation due to unrecorded vaccination timing and potential confounding. The findings have implications for cervical cancer prevention and screening, particularly in populations with low vaccination rates.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. This study aimed to evaluate factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 246 women undergoing colposcopy from January 2014 to January 2024. The study focused on women with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ and compared them with those without such lesions.
analysis_en.methods: HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. HPV status and cytological findings differed significantly between women with CIN2+ and CIN2− (both p < 0.001).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology are important factors in the development of CIN2+. This information can inform cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies, particularly in populations where HPV vaccination rates are low.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The timing of vaccination relative to HPV exposure was not recorded, and the association with lack of HPV vaccination may reflect unmeasured confounding parameters. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: 女性在进行宫颈镜检查时与活检证实的高危级宫颈病变(CIN2+)相关的因素:人乳头瘤病毒感染、疫苗接种状态和细胞学的作用
source_body_en: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. HPV infection, cytological abnormalities, and HPV vaccination status may be associated with CIN2+. This study evaluated factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2 + in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 246 women undergoing colposcopy, from January 2014 to January 2024 were included. HPV was detected using the PaxView ® Kit. CIN2 + was defined as histopathologically confirmed CIN2, CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ, or invasive cervical cancer. HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+. adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Results Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. HPV status and cytological findings differed significantly between women with CIN2 + and CIN2− (both p < 0.001). HPV16/18 was more frequent among women with CIN2 + than CIN2− (56.0% vs. 28.6%), whereas HPV-negative results were less frequent (18.0% vs. Similarly, HSIL cytology (38.0% vs. 10.7%) and lack of HPV vaccination (42.0% vs. 16.8%) were more common in the CIN2 + group. In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+. Age, marital status and other high-risk HPV genotypes were not significantly associated with CIN2+. Conclusion In this Iranian colposcopy population, HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology were independently associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+. Lack of HPV vaccination was also associated with higher odds of CIN2+, but this finding should be interpreted cautiously, as the timing of vaccination relative to HPV exposure was not recorded and the association may reflect unmeasured confounding parameters. Prospective studies focusing on vaccination timing and pre-vaccination HPV status are needed to clarify this association.

title: Immediate Risk of Cervical Precancer and Primary Triage Strategies for Women with Non- 16/18 High-Risk HPV Infection and ASC-US/LSIL Cytology: A Real-World Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Objective We evaluated the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes in women with atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) cytology, and developed a risk-based primary triage strategy. We also characterized the regional epidemiological features of HPV infection in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024. Methods Based on defined eligibility criteria, this study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo from 2019 to 2024. Colposcopy and histopathological biopsy were performed based on HPV and liquid-based cytology (TCT) findings. We used lowest-attribution (minimum), any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to evaluate the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2 + under ASC-US and LSIL cytology. Finally, we formulated a risk-stratified clinical triage framework by integrating recent evidence on extended HPV genotyping. Results Of 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 identified as the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases. Across both ASC-US and LSIL cytology, HPV31 conferred the highest immediate risk of CIN2 + among all non-16/18 genotypes. Conclusion Although non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes predominate among HPV-positive women, their immediate risks of CIN2 + are highly heterogeneous. A uniform management protocol for managing non-16/18 hrHPV infections wastes medical resources. We propose a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology: direct colposcopy for high-risk genotypes (HPV31, 33, 52, and 58); conservative follow-up for low-risk genotypes (HPV39, 56, 66, and 68); and secondary triage using biomarkers (e.g., DNA methylation, p16/Ki-67 dual staining) or cytology for intermediate-risk genotypes. This framework is designed for initial, immediate triage and does not replace long-term longitudinal surveillance for specific genotypes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV genotypes in women with ASC-US and LSIL cytology, and to develop a risk-based primary triage strategy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This real-world cross-sectional study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024, focusing on those with ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis.methods: The study used lowest-attribution, any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to assess the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2+ under ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis.main_results: Of the 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 being the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes have highly heterogeneous immediate risks of CIN2+ and proposed a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of a risk-stratified clinical triage framework for managing HPV infections in women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology, potentially improving resource allocation and patient outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the lack of longitudinal data, which may affect the interpretation of immediate risk. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) associated with non-16/18 high-risk HPV genotypes in women with ASC-US and LSIL cytology, and developed a risk-based triage strategy. Conducted in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024, the cross-sectional study enrolled 511,133 women, with 50,320 testing HPV-positive. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% of all HPV-positive cases, and HPV31 was identified as the highest risk genotype. The authors proposed a three-tiered triage strategy based on extended genotyping, recommending direct colposcopy for high-risk genotypes, conservative follow-up for low-risk genotypes, and secondary triage using biomarkers or cytology for intermediate-risk genotypes. The study highlights the heterogeneity of risk among non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and suggests a more tailored approach to triage. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to infer causality or long-term outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 我们评估了在ASC-US(意义未明的非典型鳞状细胞)和LSIL(低级别鳞状上皮内病变)细胞学检查的女性中,非16/18型高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)基因型对宫颈高级别上皮内瘤变(CIN2+)的即时风险,并制定了基于风险的初级分流策略。我们还描述了2019年至2024年间中国宁波地区人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染的流行病学特征。方法 根据定义的纳入标准,本研究纳入了2019年至2024年期间参与宁波宫颈癌筛查的511,133名女性。根据HPV和液基细胞学(TCT)检查结果进行阴道镜检查和组织病理学活检。我们使用最低归因、任意归因和分层归因模型来评估非16/18型hrHPV基因型的分布及其在ASC-US和LSIL细胞学检查下进展为CIN2+的即时风险。最后,我们通过整合最新的扩展HPV基因型证据,制定了一个基于风险的临床分流框架。结果 在511,133名接受筛查的女性中,有50,320名(9.84%)HPV阳性,其中HPV52、58和16是主要的基因型。非16/18型hrHPV占所有HPV阳性病例的84.18%(42,357/50,320)。在ASC-US和LSIL细胞学检查中,HPV31在所有非16/18型基因型中对CIN2+的即时风险最高。结论 尽管非16/18型hrHPV基因型在HPV阳性女性中占主导地位,但它们进展为CIN2+的即时风险高度异质。对非16/18型hrHPV感染采用统一的管理方案会浪费医疗资源。我们提出了一种三级、基于扩展基因型的分流策略,用于ASC-US/LSIL细胞学检查的女性:对高风险基因型(HPV31、33、52和58)直接进行阴道镜检查;对低风险基因型(HPV39、56、66和68)采取保守随访;对中等风险基因型则使用生物标志物(如DNA甲基化、p16/Ki-67双染色)或细胞学进行二次分流。该框架旨在进行初始的即时分流,不替代特定基因型的长期纵向监测监测。

title: High-risk human papillomavirus detection across the cervical disease spectrum in Abuja, Nigeria: a comparative cross-sectional study
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in Nigeria, yet data on high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) across the cervical disease spectrum are limited in Abuja. We conducted a hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study of 101 women aged [≥]25 years at Federal Medical Centre, Abuja: 59 with negative cytology (NILM) and 42 with cervical lesions, comprising 23 low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL), 8 high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), and 11 invasive cervical cancers. Cervical specimens were tested using the Atila ScreenFire assay, which reports four pooled hrHPV target groups. hrHPV DNA was detected in 37/101 women (36.6%): 30.5% (18/59) with NILM, 26.1% (6/23) with LSIL, 50.0% (4/8) with HSIL, and 81.8% (9/11) with invasive cervical cancer (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact p=0.005). Compared with NILM, invasive cervical cancer was associated with approximately tenfold higher odds of hrHPV detection (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 10.25, 95% CI 2.01-52.28; age-adjusted OR 9.90, 95% CI 1.87-52.38). The HPV31/33/35/52/58 target group was detected most frequently overall (12.9%), followed by HPV16 and HPV18/45 (10.9% each), and HPV39/51/56/59/68 (5.9%). Cervical specimens were tested using the Atila ScreenFire assay, which identifies four pooled hrHPV target groups. The results showed that hrHPV was detected in 36.6% of participants, with significantly higher rates in invasive cervical cancer compared to NILM. title: Differential effect of obesity on cervical neoplastic progression and human papillomavirus persistence: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: The role of obesity in human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence and the development of cervical neoplasia remains incompletely understood. This study evaluates the independent effects of obesity, smoking, and age on high-risk HPV persistence and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia [CIN]2+), and assesses whether obesity improves prediction of CIN2+. This retrospective cohort study included 445 women who underwent high-risk HPV testing between December 2023 and December 2025. HPV persistence was defined as detection of the same HPV genotype in at least two consecutive tests performed ≥ 12 months apart. Body mass index was categorized as non-obese (<30 kg/m2) or obese (≥30 kg/m2). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of HPV persistence and CIN2+. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to compare a baseline model including age and smoking with an extended model additionally including obesity. Persistent HPV infection was identified in 59 women (13.3%). Smoking was a strong independent predictor of HPV persistence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 13.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.54–26.09; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with persistence (aOR: 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.023). Obesity was not independently associated with HPV persistence. CIN2+ was detected in 95 women (21.3%). Obesity was independently associated with CIN2+ (aOR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.14–3.38; p = 0.015), whereas smoking and age were not significant predictors. The addition of obesity modestly improved discrimination for CIN2+ prediction (area under the curve [AUC] 0.545 vs. Smoking and age are key determinants of HPV persistence, whereas obesity appears to be associated primarily with cervical neoplastic progression rather than viral persistence. The modest increase in AUC suggests limited but measurable predictive contribution of obesity to CIN2+ risk.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of obesity on HPV persistence and cervical neoplastic progression. It evaluates the independent effects of obesity, smoking, and age on high-risk HPV persistence and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+). The findings indicate that smoking and increasing age are strong predictors of HPV persistence, while obesity is independently associated with CIN2+ progression. The study highlights the potential role of obesity in cervical neoplastic progression rather than viral persistence, and suggests that its inclusion in predictive models may offer limited but measurable improvement. The research contributes to understanding the complex interplay between lifestyle factors and HPV-related diseases, with implications for targeted surveillance and risk assessment strategies.

source_body_en: The role of obesity in human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence and the development of cervical neoplasia remains incompletely understood. This study evaluates the independent effects of obesity, smoking, and age on high-risk HPV persistence and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia [CIN]2+), and assesses whether obesity improves prediction of CIN2+. This retrospective cohort study included 445 women who underwent high-risk HPV testing between December 2023 and December 2025. HPV persistence was defined as detection of the same HPV genotype in at least two consecutive tests performed ≥ 12 months apart. Body mass index was categorized as non-obese (<30 kg/m2) or obese (≥30 kg/m2). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of HPV persistence and CIN2+. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to compare a baseline model including age and smoking with an extended model additionally including obesity. Persistent HPV infection was identified in 59 women (13.3%). Smoking was a strong independent predictor of HPV persistence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 13.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.54–26.09; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with persistence (aOR: 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.023). Obesity was not independently associated with HPV persistence. CIN2+ was detected in 95 women (21.3%). Obesity was independently associated with CIN2+ (aOR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.14–3.38; p = 0.015), whereas smoking and age were not significant predictors. The addition of obesity modestly improved discrimination for CIN2+ prediction (area under the curve [AUC] 0.545 vs. Smoking and age are key determinants of HPV persistence, whereas obesity appears to be associated primarily with cervical neoplastic progression rather than viral persistence. The modest increase in AUC suggests limited but measurable predictive contribution of obesity to CIN2+ risk.

title: A Community Engaged Feasibility Study of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling for Cervical Cancer Screening in Sexual and Gender Minority People
abstract: Background and Objectives: We investigated the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) in sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians. Methods: We conducted a descriptive qualitative study using virtual interviews to investigate socioecological factors influencing CCS and the feasibility and acceptability of at-home hrHPV self-sampling for primary CCS. Criterion and snowball sampling were used. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic approach and team member consensus to identify salient themes. Results: Nineteen participants completed hrHPV self-sampling and qualitative interviews in 2022–2023. The 6 overarching themes identified were cervical cancer screening perceptions, prior negative healthcare experiences, desirability of hrHPV self-sampling, completing hrHPV self-sampling, concerns about hrHPV self-sampling, and reasons for study participation. Conclusion: At-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase CCS in SGM people. Individuals should be reassured that self-sampling is an effective method for primary CCS and that they are likely to be able to collect a sample that will yield accurate results. To maximize the possibility of CCS completion by SGM individuals, healthcare providers and healthcare environments must be affirming, culturally competent, and informed partners throughout the CCS process.

abstract_zh: 背景和目标:我们调查了肯塔基州性少数群体 (SGM) 家庭自我采样 宫颈癌 筛查 (CCS) 对高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 的可接受性和可行性。方法:我们利用虚拟访谈进行了一项描述性定性研究,以调查影响 CCS 的社会生态因素以及家庭 hrHPV 自我采样用于原发性 CCS 的可行性和可接受性。使用标准抽样和滚雪球抽样。使用混合归纳演绎主题方法和团队成员共识来分析数据,以确定显着主题。结果:19 名参与者在 2022-2023 年完成了 hrHPV 自我采样和定性访谈。确定的 6 个首要主题是 宫颈癌 筛查认知、既往负面医疗经历、hrHPV 自我采样的可取性、完成 hrHPV 自我采样、对 hrHPV 自我采样的担忧以及参与研究的原因。结论:家庭 hrHPV 自我采样是一种有前景的干预措施,可增加 SGM 人群的 CCS。应让个人放心,自我取样是主要 CCS 的有效方法,并且他们很可能能够收集产生准确结果的样本。为了最大限度地提高 SGM 个人完成 CCS 的可能性,医疗保健提供者和医疗保健环境必须在整个 CCS 过程中成为肯定的、具有文化能力和知情的合作伙伴。

title: Association of HPV Infection with Vaginal Microecology and Abnormal Cervical Cytology: Dose–Response Effects of Viral Load in a Cross-Sectional Study of 7,997 Women in Tianmen, China

However, the contribution of the vaginal microenvironment to HPV acquisition and cervical carcinogenesis is not well characterised. We evaluated independent associations between vaginal microecological indicators and HPV infection and explored the dose–response relationship between HPV viral load and cervical cytological abnormalities. Methods This cross-sectional study included 7,997 women who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping and vaginal microecological assessment at The First People's Hospital of Tianmen between June 2024 and June 2026; 6,562 (82.06%) also underwent thin-layer cytology (TCT). title: Validation of Immunoscore for Prognostic Stratification in HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Cancer: An International Multicenter Study
abstract: PURPOSE: Optimizing treatment in HPV-associated OPSCC remains challenging, as current TNM- and smoking-based risk stratification inadequately captures tumor biological heterogeneity, highlighting the need for more prognostic biomarkers. We report the first validation of the Immunoscore (IS) in HPV-associated OPSCC. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We analyzed 191 HPV-associated (p16+ and HPV DNA/RNA+) OPSCC patients from an international multicenter cohort (2015-2024), including a French monocentric retrospective training cohort (n = 48) and three validation cohorts: French monocentric retrospective (n = 48), French multicenter prospective (n = 50), and US multicenter retrospective (n = 45). IS quantified CD3+ and CD8+ densities in tumor cores and invasive margins, with cut-offs defined in the training cohort and validated across cohorts. Associations with disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and time to recurrence (TTR) were assessed, alongside 3'RNA-seq and sequential immunofluorescence profiling. RESULTS: Median age 65; 80% male; 74% smokers; 66% T1-2; 82% N0-1. IS-High patients had superior 3-year DFS across cohorts (all log-rank P < .05). Multivariable analysis identified IS-Low as the independent prognostic factor with the largest adjusted effect size for DFS (HR 9.03; 95% CI: 4.02-20.31; P < .001). The combined IS-clinical model showed better DFS prediction than the clinical-only model (C-index 0.82 vs 0.70; P < .0001). Similar results were observed for TTR and OS. IS-High tumors showed enriched lymphoid and myeloid populations, contrasting with immune-poor IS-Low tumors. CONCLUSIONS: IS outperformed clinical variables in prognostic performance. By identifying biologically distinct risk groups, IS may enable biomarker-guided, risk-adapted treatment strategies, including treatment de-escalation and intensification.

title: Diagnostic pitfalls leading to delayed diagnosis of human papillomavirus (HPV)–independent cervical malignancies in the era of HPV-based screening: clinicopathologic analysis of diagnostic pathways
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV)–independent cervical malignancies (HPV-IDCM) are a rare but clinically important subset that may escape detection by HPV-based screening. This study investigated diagnostic pitfalls contributing to delayed HPV-IDCM diagnosis and assessed the role of cervical cytology in the diagnostic pathway. Methods: This multicenter retrospective case series was conducted as a policy research project of the Korean Society for Cytopathology. Patients with HPV-IDCM and repeated abnormal cytologic findings before definitive histologic diagnosis were identified. Clinical, cytologic, histologic, and HPV test results were reviewed to identify factors associated with diagnostic delay. Results: Four patients were included, with a median age of 74 years (range, 62 to 79 years). Histologic diagnoses comprised three HPV-independent gastric-type adenocarcinomas and one HPV-independent squamous cell carcinoma. The median interval from the first abnormal cytologic finding to definitive diagnosis was 18.5 months (range, 11 to 30 months). Before diagnosis, all patients underwent a median of 3.5 cytologic examinations (range, 3 to 5). Associated factors included repeatedly negative HPV test results (3/4), nondiagnostic biopsy or conization (2/4), delayed tissue evaluation despite persistent cytologic abnormalities (1/4), deeply located endocervical lesions (3/4), and a concurrent HPV-associated squamous lesion (1/4). Re-review identified atypical or malignant cells in all cases, indicating that the delay did not result from failure of cytologic detection. Conclusions: HPV-IDCM remain vulnerable to delayed diagnosis in the era of HPV-based screening. Persistent abnormal cytologic findings should not be dismissed solely because HPV test results are negative. Careful correlation of cytologic, clinical, and histologic findings remains essential for timely HPV-IDCM detection.

title: Concordance of flow cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection with human papillomavirus DNA testing and cervical cytology in a cervical cancer screening cohort
abstract: Background: Overexpression of viral oncogenes E6 and E7 of high-risk (HR)–human papillomavirus (HPV) plays a key role in the progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cancer. Detection of E6/E7 mRNA may help distinguish between transient and transforming infections, thus improving cervical cancer screening accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the association of E6/E7 mRNA expression with HR-HPV infection, cervical cytology, and histologically confirmed cervical lesions and to compare its agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology. Methods: A total of 526 women undergoing cervical cancer screening between January 2023 and May 2025 were enrolled. E6/E7 mRNA expression was assessed using flow cytometry with the HPV OncoTect 3Dx E6/E7 mRNA assay and compared with HR-HPV DNA testing, cervical cytology, and available histopathologic findings from biopsy specimens. Results: Among 526 samples, eight (1.5%) tested positive for E6/E7 mRNA, compared to 30 (5.7%) HR-HPV DNA–positive and 17 (3.2%) abnormal cytology results. Median E6/E7 mRNA expression was higher in HR-HPV– positive cases and in cytologically abnormal cases. Almost perfect agreement was observed between E6/E7 mRNA results, HR-HPV DNA testing, and cytology. Histopathologic follow-up was available for nine women with cytological abnormalities ≥low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, including four CIN2 and five CIN1 cases. E6/E7 mRNA expression was markedly elevated in one CIN2 case associated with HPV16 infection (37.51%), while two CIN1 cases demonstrated high mRNA expression despite negative HPV DNA results. Conclusions: Flow-cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection showed high overall agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology in this screening cohort. Larger prospective studies with comprehensive histologic follow-up are needed to determine its clinical utility.

title: Human Papilloma Virus detection through the cobas® 4800 system in women from Lima, Peru
abstract: Aim: Determine the prevalence of high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in women from Lima between 2012 and 2013 using the Cobas 4800 test.Method: The study included 5324 women aged 30 or over, whose cervical samples underwent the Cobas 4800 molecular test.Positive samples were analyzed through liquid-based cytology.Results: The prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 15.2%.Genotype 16 was found in 16.2%, genotype 18 in 3. 1% and genotypes 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68 in 71.2%.62.8% of samples were identified without cytological changes, 19.8% with LSIL, 14% with ASCUS, 2% with HSIL, and 0.7% with ASC-H.Conclusion: The prevalence of HR-HPV in this study continues to be significant.In simple infections, the frequency of genotypes 16 and 18 stood out, and in coinfections, the group of the other twelve HPV-RA genotypes predominated.

title: Detection of Microorganisms Associated With Sexually Transmitted Infections and High-Risk HPV Genotypes in Patients Aged 20–30 Years
abstract: Uvod: Seksualno prenosive infekcije (SPI) predstavljaju značajan javnozdravstveni problem zbog učestalosti i mogućih dugoročnih komplikacija. Poseban značaj ima humani papiloma virus (HPV), čiji su visokorizični genotipovi povezani sa nastankom karcinoma grlića materice. Cilj rada: Ispitivanje učestalosti detekcije sedam mikroorganizama povezanih sa SPI i visokorizičnih genotipova HPV-a, kao i zastupljenosti njihove istovremene detekcije kod pacijenata uzrasta 20–30 godina. Materijal i metode: Istraživanjem je obuhvaćeno 50 pacijenata, 42 žene i 8 muškaraca, uzrasta 20–30 godina. Uzorci cervikalnih i uretralnih briseva prikupljeni su od 1. godine u Centru za ginekologiju i humanu reprodukciju i Klinici za urologiju VMA. Pacijenti su se javljali zbog kontrolnih pregleda ili prisutne simptomatologije. Ispitivanje je sprovedeno na klinički selektovanom uzorku, uz slučajan odabir pacijenata. Analiza je izvršena primenom dve multipleks real-time PCR metode. STD 7 testom detektovani su Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium, Mycoplasma hominis, Trichomonas vaginalis, Ureaplasma urealyticum i Ureaplasma parvum. Drugim testom izvršena je genotipizacija 14 visokorizičnih genotipova HPV-a. Istraživanje je odobrila nadležna Etička komisija VMA. Rezultati: Najmanje jedan analizirani mikroorganizam detektovan je kod 18 (36%) pacijenata, dok je visokorizični HPV detektovan kod 19 (38%). Najzastupljeniji su bili U. Dominantni HPV genotipovi bili su 16, 31, 35, 59 i 52. Kod četiri ispitanika detektovano je više HPV genotipova. Istovremena detekcija mikroorganizama i visokorizičnog HPV-a zabeležena je kod sedam pacijenata (14% - npr. parvum sa tipovima 18, 35 i 52). hominis registrovani su i kod pacijenata sa dizuričnim tegobama, bolom i peckanjem. Zaključak: Rezultati ukazuju na prisustvo mikroorganizama povezanih sa SPI i visokorizičnih genotipova HPV-a u ispitivanoj grupi. Multipleks real-time PCR predstavlja izuzetno pouzdan dijagnostički alat za istovremenu detekciju ciljnih mikroorganizama i genotipizaciju HPV-a, uz neophodnu interpretaciju nalaza u kontekstu kliničke slike.
