title: Modern Approaches in HPV-positive Oropharyngeal Cancer Screening
abstract: Oral human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a public health issue with a rising incidence over the last two decades, particularly among young adults. Oral HPV is primarily transmitted through oral-genital contact. Among the more than 200 identified strains, high-risk oncogenic types – specifically HPV-16 and HPV-18 – are strongly associated with the development of oropharyngeal cancer, particularly in the tonsils and the base of the tongue. While most infections are transient and asymptomatic, clearing within 1–2 years due to the immune system’s response, persistent infections can lead to malignant cellular transformation. This analysis aims to provide an up-to-date synthesis of data regarding the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostic methods, and prevention strategies for oral HPV infection, highlighting the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in reducing the risk of oncological complications. Diagnosis of oral HPV infection is often difficult due to the lack of specific symptoms but can be achieved through molecular tests for the detection of viral DNA. Currently, there is no standardized screening protocol for oral HPV infection, which makes prevention play an essential role. HPV vaccination, available and recommended for both girls and boys, has been shown to be effective in preventing infections with oncogenic risk strains. Other prevention measures include the use of protection during sexual intercourse and the promotion of education on HPV transmission. Oropharyngeal cancer is a malignancy affecting structures in the middle region of the pharynx, including the base of the tongue, the tonsils, the soft palate, and the posterior pharyngeal wall. In recent decades, a significant shift in the etiology of this cancer has been observed, marked by an alarming rise in cases associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection – specifically the HPV-16 strain.

title: Synthetic Biology in the Design and Development of Virus-Like Particle Vaccines
abstract: With the frequent emergence of new infectious diseases and the growing demand for precision medicine, the limitations of traditional vaccines are becoming increasingly apparent. Virus-like particles (VLPs) have become a key platform for the development of next-generation vaccines due to their combination of structural characteristics typical of natural viruses and a favorable safety profile. From the perspective of synthetic biology, this article reviews the working principles, production processes, and key construction technologies of VLP vaccines, with a focus on research progress regarding chassis protein design, engineering modification of antigen modules, optimization of linkage systems, and enhancement of structural stability. Meanwhile, the development status of marketed VLP vaccines, such as those for hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis E virus (HEV), and human papillomavirus (HPV) is summarized, and the application of VLP vaccines currently in clinical research, including those for influenza, COVID-19, and HIV is analyzed. The results demonstrate that synthetic biology has significantly enhanced the programmability, immunogenicity, and development efficiency of VLP vaccines, driving their evolution toward multivalent, intelligent, and personalized forms. However, issues such as complex antigen display, large-scale production, and the evaluation of long-term protective efficacy remain to be addressed. Future research could further integrate AI-driven protein design, novel expression systems, and precision delivery technologies to advance the clinical translation and industrial application of VLP vaccines.
journal: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences

title: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma detected in cervical pap smear: A case report and literature review
abstract: Cervical Pap smears primarily detect primary neoplasms but may also identify metastases, such as urothelial carcinoma (UC), which can be confused with primary cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). This report describes a case in a centenarian with recurrent bladder UC. The Pap smear revealed atypical cells with marked pleomorphism, anisonucleosis (≥3-fold variation), coarse chromatin, cercaria-like cells, and focal glandular differentiation. Immunocytochemistry (ICC) was positive for P63, cytokeratin 7 ( CK7), and GATA binding protein 3 ( GATA-3), negative for P16, paired box 8 ( PAX-8), and cytokeratin 20 ( CK20); P53 was wild-type, and human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA was negative. This case expands the sparse cytological literature on metastatic UC and underscores the utility of integrating clinical history, cytomorphology, ICC, and HPV testing to avoid SCC misclassification.

title: Efficacy of Cryotherapy Compared With Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure Among Women With and Without HIV in Kenya.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among Kenyan women aged 15-44. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) in women with HIV (WHIV) is more likely to progress in severity compared with women without HIV. This study assesses the results of cryotherapy or LEEP for CIN among WHIV compared with women without HIV in Western Kenya. METHODS: Eighty-six WHIV (39 cryotherapy, 47 LEEP) and 89 women without HIV (46 cryotherapy, 43 LEEP) who had follow-up within 24 months were included in this analysis. Women ineligible for cryotherapy underwent colposcopy/biopsy, and those with confirmed CIN 2/3 underwent LEEP. Women were followed every 6 months with VIA, Pap smear or colposcopy/biopsy. χ2 and Fisher exact tests were used to compare the proportions. RESULTS: There was a significant difference in overall treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (15.12% vs 5.62% p=.039). There was a significant difference in treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV who underwent cryotherapy (18% vs 2.1%, p=.021). Among patients who underwent LEEP, no difference was observed in the treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (12.8% vs 9.3%, p=.742). CONCLUSIONS: In our experience, LEEP is a more effective treatment than cryotherapy for WHIV compared with women without HIV for CIN in Western Kenya.

Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) in women with HIV (WHIV) is more likely to progress in severity compared with women without HIV. This study assesses the results of cryotherapy or LEEP for CIN among WHIV compared with women without HIV in Western Kenya. Methods Eighty-six WHIV (39 cryotherapy, 47 LEEP) and 89 women without HIV (46 cryotherapy, 43 LEEP) who had follow-up within 24 months were included in this analysis. Women ineligible for cryotherapy underwent colposcopy/biopsy, and those with confirmed CIN 2/3 underwent LEEP. Women were followed every 6 months with VIA, Pap smear or colposcopy/biopsy. χ2 and Fisher exact tests were used to compare the proportions. Results There was a significant difference in overall treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (15.12% vs 5.62% p=.039). There was a significant difference in treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV who underwent cryotherapy (18% vs 2.1%, p=.021). Among patients who underwent LEEP, no difference was observed in the treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (12.8% vs 9.3%, p=.742). Conclusions In our experience, LEEP is a more effective treatment than cryotherapy for WHIV compared with women without HIV for CIN in Western Kenya.

title: Knowledge and awareness of HPV vaccination and cervical cancer among young adults
abstract: Cervical cancer is the second leading cause of cancer related mortality especially in women in India. Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause, and effective vaccines are available for its prevention. However, awareness and knowledge about HPV and its vaccine remain low, especially among young adults. This study aims to assess their knowledge, awareness, and attitudes toward HPV, cervical cancer, and vaccination. A survey was carried out over a 6-month period from November 2024 to April 2025, following an awareness campaign. A structured questionnaire was used in individuals aged below 15, 15–20, and above 20 years. The questionnaire covered demographics, HPV and cervical cancer knowledge, awareness and attitude towards vaccination. Of the 2000 participants surveyed, 55.45% were aware of HPV vaccine, yet only 14.8% had received it. While 63.75% showed willingness for future vaccination, many cited lack of awareness, fear of side effects, and cost as barriers. Notably, 75.05% expressed interest in receiving more information, especially if recommended by healthcare providers. This study concludes that awareness of HPV vaccine is moderate in young adults and key barriers to vaccination are lack of information, cost, and fear of side effects.

title: Incremental Diagnostic Value of p16/Ki-67 Dual-Stain Immunocytochemistry in HPV-Positive Women with a Type 3 Transformation Zone: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: In women with a type 3 transformation zone (TZ3), the squamocolumnar junction is not fully visible and endocervical disease may be missed. We assessed whether p16/Ki-67 dual-stain immunocytochemistry adds diagnostic information to HPV16/18 genotyping and liquid-based cytology. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 312 HPV-positive women with colposcopically confirmed TZ3 who underwent cytology, dual staining and endocervical curettage (ECC) at one visit; ECC-detected CIN2+ was the reference standard. Nested logistic models (HPV16/18 plus cytology, with and without dual stain) were compared using the change in the area under the ROC curve (ΔAUC; AUC = probability that a woman with CIN2+ has a higher predicted risk than one without), a likelihood-ratio test and bootstrap internal validation. Results: ECC detected CIN2+ in 56 women (17.9%). Against ECC, dual-stain sensitivity was 82.1%, specificity 69.9% and negative predictive value 94.7%. Adding dual staining increased the AUC from 0.760 to 0.863 (ΔAUC 0.103, 95% CI 0.055–0.163; p < 0.001; optimism-corrected AUCs 0.751 and 0.855). Eight of ten dual-stain-negative CIN2+ cases had HPV16/18 and/or ASC-H/HSIL cytology. Conclusions: Dual staining improved statistical discrimination for ECC-detected CIN2+ beyond genotype and cytology. This does not establish clinical benefit; the test should not be used alone to omit ECC and requires external validation.

title: Phenolic Hydroxyl-Containing Lipid Nanoparticles Enable Codelivery of HPV Peptide Antigens and Manganese Adjuvant for Cancer Immunotherapy.
abstract: Therapeutic peptide vaccines against HPV-associated cancers are often limited by insufficient immunogenicity and inefficient intracellular delivery. Here, we develop a phenolic hydroxyl-containing lipid nanoparticle (EMT@LNP) as a nanomedicine platform for the coordinated codelivery of HPV16 E6/E7 peptide antigens and manganese (Mn2+) adjuvant. Distinct from conventional electrostatic loading strategies, EMT@LNP exploits hydrogen-bonding interactions between phenolic hydroxyl groups and peptide antigens, enabling charge-independent loading of peptides with diverse physicochemical properties, while coordination interactions between phenolic moieties and Mn2+ allow the simultaneous incorporation of immunostimulatory adjuvants. This dual-interaction-driven design integrates antigen delivery and innate immune activation within a single nanostructure. Functionally, EMT@LNP enhances antigen uptake and promotes dendritic cell maturation, accompanied by activation of STING-associated signaling, as indicated by increased phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3. In vivo, EMT@LNP facilitates efficient delivery to draining lymph nodes and prolongs antigen retention following intramuscular administration. In a therapeutic TC-1 tumor model, EMT@LNP elicits potent antitumor immune responses, characterized by enhanced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and reduced immunosuppressive cell populations, leading to significant tumor growth inhibition without observable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study presents a nanobiotechnology strategy that combines charge-independent peptide loading with metal-ion-mediated immune activation, providing a versatile and potentially translatable platform for therapeutic vaccination against HPV-associated malignancies.

title: Light-based therapies for multidomain symptom burden in people living with HIV: a scoping review of clinical evidence, molecular immunology, and safety boundaries
abstract: People living with HIV (PLWH) may continue to experience interacting mucocutaneous lesions, pain, pruritus, oral infection, impaired healing, constitutional symptoms and reduced quality of life despite effective antiretroviral therapy (ART). Light-based interventions can modify local pathology and immune signaling, but their clinical and mechanistic evidence is dispersed across dermatology, dentistry, infectious disease, oncology and apheresis. This scoping review was structured using JBI guidance and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and SinoMed were searched from inception to 9 August 2026. Clinical sources were charted by population, modality, optical parameters, symptom domain, efficacy, safety, immune or virological outcomes and treatment burden. Design-specific appraisal used RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized comparative intervention studies and JBI checklists for other eligible designs. Clinical evidence directly obtained in PLWH was synthesized separately from contextual photobiology and hypothesis-generating mechanistic links. Fifty-five evidence sources, 21 Chinese and 34 English, represented 54 unique cohorts. Evidence clustered in anogenital HPV-related disease, dermatologic disease and ultraviolet safety, oral conditions, Kaposi sarcoma and systemic or psychological interventions. Across modalities, randomized evidence was mostly judged as having some concerns, non-randomized comparative studies commonly had moderate-to-serious risk of bias, and uncontrolled or historical reports had substantial methodological limitations. No modality was supported by high-certainty clinical evidence. ALA-based photodynamic therapy (PDT) had the most concentrated, but still low-certainty, support for local lesion control in anogenital disease. Oral antimicrobial PDT, photobiomodulation and UVB had narrower or very-low-certainty support. A contemporary sham-controlled vascular-PBM trial did not show virological or immunological superiority. The molecular synthesis distinguishes direct PLWH observations from contextual pathways and hypothesis-generating links. Light-based therapies should be positioned as adjunctive, symptom-directed interventions. ALA-PDT for anogenital HPV-related disease has the strongest relative signal, but confidence remains low because of risk of bias, heterogeneity and limited follow-up. Oral aPDT may be considered adjunctive, whereas PBM, lesion-directed Kaposi therapy, extracorporeal photopheresis and bright-light therapy remain experimental or very low certainty in PLWH. Current evidence does not support vascular PBM for systemic immune restoration or virological control. UVB requires an explicit local HIV-transcription safety boundary. No evidence supports HIV eradication. https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/WNX84 .

title: Immune protection against anogenital HPV in Rwandan women with and without HIV following the introduction of quadrivalent HPV vaccination.
abstract: Abstract Introduction Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines have demonstrated population effectiveness in preventing cervical cancer. Evidence for protection of women with HIV (WWH) is lacking. In 2011, Rwanda introduced quadrivalent HPV vaccination nationally, primarily targeting girls in grade 6, providing an opportunity to evaluate its long-term effectiveness in WWH compared to women without HIV (WWoH) Methods Data from 3,058 of 3,148 (97.1%) Rwandan women with complete results from four sub-cohorts recruited and enrolled were analyzed: 769 WWoH born before 1996, 755 WWoH born 1996 or more recently, 773 WWH born before 1996, and 761 WWH born 1996 or more recently. We tested vaginal and anal specimens for high-risk HPV genotypes. We used self-report of HPV vaccination and measured anti-HPV16 antibodies levels by HPV16 VLP ELISA as HPV vaccination proxies to examine the protective effects, using logistic regression, of HPV vaccination on vaginal and/or anal (combined, “anogenital”) HPV16 and/or HPV18 (HPV16/18). Results Self-reported HPV vaccination (vs. not) (adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=2.71, 95%CI=2.29-3.21) was most strongly positively, and WWH (vs. WWoH) (aOR=0.68, 95%CI=0.60-0.78) was most strongly negatively, associated with higher anti-HPV16 antibody levels. Anogenital HPV16/18 prevalence decreased from 11.0% to 2.5% in those with the lowest to highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels, respectively (ptrend<0.001). The highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels was associated with lower anogenital HPV16/18 (aOR=0.23, 95%CI=0.13-0.38); similar associations were observed for the highest quartile in WWH (aOR=0.23; 95%CI=0.12-0.46) as in WWoH (aOR=0.24, 95%CI=0.10-0.58). Conclusion WWH who were likely vaccinated against HPV vaccination had lower prevalence of anogenital HPV16/18.

title: Reproductive and Gynecological Factors Associated with Cervical Pathology: A Review of Current Evidence
abstract: Cervical pathology remains an important issue in gynecology, with its development associated with a combination of infectious, reproductive, hormonal, and behavioral factors. This review aimed to summarize current evidence on reproductive and gynecological factors associated with pathological changes of the cervix. Particular attention was given to reproductive history, age at sexual debut, parity, pregnancies and childbirth, hormonal contraceptive use, sexually transmitted infections, and other conditions that may affect cervical health. Human papillomavirus infection was considered a major factor in the development of cervical intraepithelial lesions, particularly when combined with other adverse factors. Current evidence suggests that most of these characteristics should not be considered in isolation, as their significance may depend on persistent HPV infection, reproductive behavior, and a woman's gynecological health. Identification of such combinations may contribute to defining higher-risk groups, individualizing preventive follow-up, and improving the timely detection of cervical abnormalities. The available evidence supports the inclusion of reproductive and gynecological history in a comprehensive approach to the prevention of cervical pathology.

title: Parental knowledge, health-worker information and safety concerns as correlates of HPV vaccine uptake among girls aged 9 to 14 years in Kogi State, Nigeria: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background. Nigeria added the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to routine immunization in October 2023, but uptake remains low, and evidence from north-central states is scarce. We estimated parent-reported uptake and correlates among parents of girls aged 9 to 14 years in three Kogi State local government areas (LGAs). In a cross-sectional survey, we interviewed 336 parents and guardians in Lokoja, Igalamela, and Ibaji; we analyzed 329 with at least one eligible daughter. The outcome was the report of at least one vaccinated daughter. Knowledge was the count of nine awareness items answered yes. With 61 vaccinated parents, associations were estimated with Firth-penalized logistic regression, and 30 bivariate tests were corrected for multiplicity. Sixty-one parents (18.5%, 95% CI 14.7 to 23.1) reported a vaccinated daughter; 118 of 326 (36.2%) had never heard of the vaccine. Uptake rose from 0.9% to a knowledge score of 0 to 48.6% at 7 to 9. After adjustment, each additional item known (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.56, 95% CI 1.36 to 1.82) and naming a health worker as the main source versus other sources (aOR 3.85, 1.89 to 8.32) were associated with higher odds of uptake, and concern about side effects with lower odds (aOR 0.40, 0.18 to 0.88). Education, income, religion, and LGA were not independently associated. Uptake was concentrated among informed parents, those informed by health workers, and those not worried about side effects. Vaccination itself exposes parents to information, so these associations are not causal. Health-worker communication and safety messaging merit priority.

title: Desafios da implementação do exame DNA-HPV no rastreamento do câncer do colo do útero na atenção primária à saúde e o papel do biomédico: revisão de literatura Challenges in implementing HPV DNA testing for cervical cancer screening in primary health care and the role of the biomedical scientist: a literature review
abstract: This article analyzes the implementation of human papillomavirus DNA testing (HPV DNA test) as the primary screening method for cervical cancer in primary care, its advances and challenges, and how the literature addresses the role of the biomedical scientist. It is a narrative review of 17 publications from 2021 to 2026, purposively selected: 11 reviews, five studies with epidemiological or health service data, and one announcement from the Brazilian Ministry of Health. The reviews describe the test as more sensitive than cytology (90% to 95% versus 50% to 70%), with a five-year interval after a negative result and self-sampling, but with lower specificity and higher cost, which requires triage of positive cases. A national estimate points to a shortfall of biopsies and excisions in all states and of colposcopies in almost all. Training and infrastructure are cited as requirements, but no publication on screening mentions the biomedical scientist. It is concluded that the literature analyzed describes the HPV DNA test as an advance whose implementation requires a diagnostic confirmation and treatment network, staff training and equitable access, and that the role of the biomedical scientist, only inferred from the laboratory steps of the test, was not addressed in this set.
authors: Ilecari de Fatima Leonel da Cruz Gimenez

title: Restricted HPV persistence after clinical non-detection: an operational framework for evidence and validation
abstract: HPV test results describe detection at a sampled site and time, but do not establish whether an infection has been eradicated. Existing latency models already accommodate basal epithelial persistence, immune control, and later reactivation. We use restricted persistent infection as an operational refinement of these concepts: retention of replication-capable HPV genomes in a defined epithelial compartment without demonstrated sustained productive infection. Human tissue studies have detected focal HPV DNA in cervices without evidence of productive or transforming lesions, although they have not established a continuous link between intact episomes, the cells carrying them, and later reactivation. Animal experiments and cell-based studies address different parts of this mechanism and are assessed separately. The framework distinguishes biological states from observed test results, separates productive infection from intermittent DNA detection, and specifies competing explanations for type-specific redetection. We propose complementary tissue-localization, genome-structure, and functional assays, together with longitudinal sampling and exposure assessment. Viral continuity would be assessed through whole-genome sequencing, repeated sampling, tissue localization, and exposure histories. Quantitative study examples define the populations, detection performance, and event frequencies against which particular predictions could be tested. Tissue studies would estimate the prevalence of retained replication-capable genomes, while longitudinal studies would assess their relationship to subsequent type-specific redetection.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Viral etiology of acute non-obstructive pyelonephritis: current data and diagnostic perspectives
abstract: Acute non-obstructive pyelonephritis (ANP) remains a relevant problem in urology due to the rise of antimicrobial resistance, frequent recurrences, and the risk of chronic kidney disease. The classical bacterial model does not explain cases of sterile urine cultures, lack of response to antibiotics, or seasonality of the disease. To summarize current data on the role of viral infections, i.e. human papillomavirus (HPV), herpes simplex virus (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), in the etiology and pathogenesis of ANP; to analyze the mechanisms of viral-bacterial interaction, and to outline future directions for diagnosis. Materials & methods. A review of Russian and international publications was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and eLibrary databases. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large clinical trials over the past 10–15 years; fundamental works from earlier periods were included selectively. It has been established that HSV, CMV, EBV, and HPV play an etiological role in the development of acute non-obstructive pyelonephritis. HPV-associated cystitis with pathomorphological verification (koilocytosis) serves as a proven model of viral involvement of the urinary system. Viral-bacterial synergy is realized through urothelial damage, suppression of antimicrobial peptides, cytokine storm, and molecular mimicry. Virus-associated ANP is characterized by a more severe course, a higher rate of recurrences, and an increased risk of chronic kidney disease. Accumulated evidence suggests a probable etiological role of viral infection (HSV, CMV, EBV, HPV) in the development of ANP. However, current clinical guidelines do not include virological diagnostics, which justifies the need to develop new diagnostic algorithms using polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

title: Vacinação contra o HPV em adolescentes no Nordeste brasileiro: análise da cobertura vacinal e tendências temporais HPV vaccination among adolescents in Northeast Brazil: analysis of vaccination coverage and temporal trends
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major public health concern, associated with the development of several types of cancer, particularly cervical cancer, and HPV vaccination is provided free of charge by Brazil’s Unified Health System. This study aimed to analyze the evolution of HPV vaccination among adolescents in the Northeast region of Brazil from January 2014 to October 2026, according to state, sex, and age group. This is an ecological, retrospective, time-series study based on aggregated secondary data from the National Immunization Program Information System, made available by the Department of Informatics of the Unified Health System (DATASUS), and from the Ministry of Health vaccination coverage panel, covering the nine states of the region. Temporal trends were assessed using the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope. Between 2014 and 2022, the number of doses administered in the Northeast decreased from 2,337,309 to 1,067,969. In 2026, based on data available through October, regional vaccination coverage was 73.2 percent, higher among girls (77.8 percent) than among boys (68.8 percent). Ceará had the highest coverage (81.2 percent) and Maranhão the lowest (68.2 percent), and no state reached 90 percent coverage in either sex. It is concluded that HPV vaccination in the Northeast shows territorial and sex-based inequalities, highlighting the need to strengthen vaccination strategies, active outreach, and health education, particularly among boys and younger adolescents.

title: Low-Grade Cervical Lesion Associated with Rare HPV Genotype 53: Implications for Screening and Risk Stratification
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the principal etiological factor in cervical intraepithelial lesions, with high-risk genotypes such as HPV 16 and 18 being most commonly implicated. However, the clinical significance of less common genotypes, including HPV 53, remains incompletely understood. HPV 53 is classified among probable high-risk types, but its independent role in cervical cytological abnormalities is still under investigation. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 46-year-old woman who presented for routine cervical screening. Cytological examination of the Pap smear revealed features consistent with low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), characterized by koilocytic changes, nuclear enlargement, and mild nuclear atypia. Reflex HPV genotyping demonstrated positivity for HPV 53 as the sole detected genotype, while all other high-risk and low-risk HPV types were negative. Discussion: The detection of HPV 53 as an isolated genotype in association with LSIL is uncommon and raises important considerations regarding its pathogenic potential. Although HPV 53 is not among the most prevalent highrisk types, emerging evidence suggests a possible association with low-grade lesions and, in rare instances, progression. This case highlights the importance of recognizing non-16/18 HPV genotypes in cervical screening programs and underscores the need for careful follow-up and risk stratification according to current guidelines. Conclusion: This case emphasizes the potential clinical relevance of HPV 53 in cervical cytological abnormalities. Isolated HPV 53 infection may be associated with LSIL and warrants appropriate surveillance. Further studies are needed to clarify its oncogenic risk and implications for patient management.

title: Long-term trends and future projections of cervical cancer burden in China, 1990–2023: a Global Burden of Disease 2023 analysis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge among women in China. This study aimed to comprehensively assess long-term trends and future projections of cervical cancer burden in China. METHODS: Data on cervical cancer in China from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from Global Burden of Disease Study2023. Prevalence, incidence, deaths, years lived with disability (YLDs), years of life lost (YLLs), disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) were analyzed. Temporal trends were evaluated using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and Joinpoint regression. Das Gupta decomposition quantified the contributions of population growth, aging, and epidemiological change. Nordpred was used to project deaths and DALYs from 2024 to 2045. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, prevalent cervical cancer cases increased from 445,795 (95% uncertainty interval [UI]=301,749-642,609) to 752,306 (95% UI=481,273 to 1,011,544). YLDs increased by 62%, whereas YLLs decreased by 4%. Overall DALYs decreased slightly from 1,457,115 (95% UI=1,070,025 to 2,064,940) to 1,430,054 (95% UI=896,628 to 1,874,757), while deaths increased by 16%. Age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR) declined from 294.14 to 132.72 per 100,000 population, with an EAPC of -2.43 (95% confidence interval=-2.54 to -2.33). Decomposition showed that population aging and growth offset favorable epidemiological changes, and projections suggested continued declines in ASDR with relatively stable deaths through 2045. CONCLUSION: Despite sustained declines in ASRs, the absolute burden of cervical cancer in China remains considerable due to demographic shifts. These findings underscore the urgent need to strengthen human papillomavirus vaccination coverage and expand equitable cervical cancer screening programs.

Temporal trends were evaluated using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and Joinpoint regression. Das Gupta decomposition quantified the contributions of population growth, aging, and epidemiological change. Nordpred was used to project deaths and DALYs from 2024 to 2045. Overall DALYs decreased slightly from 1,457,115 (95% UI=1,070,025 to 2,064,940) to 1,430,054 (95% UI=896,628 to 1,874,757), while deaths increased by 16%. Age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR) declined from 294.14 to 132.72 per 100,000 population, with an EAPC of -2.43 (95% confidence interval=-2.54 to -2.33). CONCLUSION: Despite sustained declines in ASRs, the absolute burden of cervical cancer in China remains considerable due to demographic shifts. These findings underscore the urgent need to strengthen human papillomavirus vaccination coverage and expand equitable cervical cancer screening programs.

title: Editorial: Strategies to improve awareness and management of cancer risk factors and screenings
abstract: early warning signs of cancer appears to be insufficient. Public knowledge about cancer is important because 44% of cancer deaths are attributable to modifiable risk factors (3) and because patients diagnosed at an early stage have better treatment outcomes (4). The study by Sauer et al. (5) assessed the behaviors, attitudes, and awareness regarding skin cancer among Polish medical and non-medical students. The students' knowledge of skin cancer, selfexamination, and sun protection was adequate. However, medical students demonstrated a higher level of knowledge than non-medical students. Women were more likely to use sunscreen than men. Knowledge scores correlated significantly with sunscreen use. (6) showed that education was highly effective in improving students' knowledge of melanoma prevention and recognition. The authors introduced web-based e-learning tools and peer education among high school students aged 14-16 years. Students completed pre-and post-intervention questionnaires. Knowledge of the ABCDE rule rose from 7.5% to 96.6%, and knowledge of the ugly duckling sign rose from 9.1% to 91.2%. In an international study of almost 1,000 students, Bordakiewicz et al. (7) found that young people were aware of common cancer risk factors (cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, sunbathing or tanning bed use, exposure to ionizing radiation, diet, and occupational exposure to carcinogens). However, there were gaps in knowledge of other risk factors, such as low physical activity, viral infections, and hormonal contraception. Notably, the students overestimated the role of genetic factors. As in the study by Sauer et al. (5), medical students in this study demonstrated more accurate knowledge about cancer than non-medical students. Additionally, students with a family history of cancer knew more about cancer than those without such a history.Better-educated people are more likely to pay attention to their own health, perform selfexamination, and participate in screening. The study by Garai et al. (8) showed that half of the female students performed breast self-examination. Students with better knowledge of breast cancer prevention were more likely to practice breast self-examination. Information from gynecologists and family members played a crucial role in adherence to breast selfexamination. A family history of breast cancer was significantly associated with practicing breast self-examination. Higher self-efficacy was also an important factor in this study. In a study by Jiang et al. (9), better knowledge was associated with more positive attitudes toward human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. The authors showed that patients who were younger, lived in urban areas, had higher levels of education and income, and had better knowledge of cervical cancer and HPV were more willing to be vaccinated. However, of the more than 1,000 women studied, only 28% had been vaccinated. Similarly, in the study by Kandasamy et al. (10), only 21% of the women surveyed in Saudi Arabia had been vaccinated against HPV.Overall, 66% of the participants demonstrated good knowledge of HPV and cervical cancer prevention. Nevertheless, the women surveyed were not familiar with cervical cancer screening and did not participate in it regularly. The authors identified lack of knowledge and discomfort as the main barriers to undergoing a Pap test. Women who were older, less educated, or unmarried had less knowledge and more negative attitudes toward gynecological examination.Identifying effective ways to encourage participation in screening is therefore essential. (11) conducted a qualitative study to assess participants' attitudes and preferences regarding screening, using kidney cancer as an example. Patients prioritized test accuracy but also preferred procedures that were convenient, safe, non-invasive, and minimally painful. The results indicated that factors motivating patients to participate in cancer screening included health needs, social support, risk awareness, recommendations from authoritative sources, and the availability of screening. Physicians were perceived as the best and most reliable source of information; despite having access to other sources, patients still trusted physicians the most. this analysis, the authors emphasized the need for a comprehensive and region-specific approach to breast cancer control. This effort should focus on improving access to screening and advanced treatment in less developed regions, implementing tailored prevention strategies, and addressing significant modifiable risk factors, such as an unhealthy diet, a sedentary lifestyle, and obesity. (15) performed a similar analysis of GBD 2021 data for laryngeal cancer. Although the incidence of laryngeal cancer, unlike that of breast cancer, has been steadily declining, the authors emphasized the need to focus on groups that are particularly susceptible to this cancer. Cigarette smokers, as well as men younger than 75 years and those older than 85 years, should be targeted as key groups for prevention and closer surveillance.The results of these two analyses underscore the urgent need to develop global and regional public health strategies and policies regarding cancer prevention and screening.With advances in science and technology, artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in oncology. ( 16) presented a narrative review that comprehensively explored the potential of AI in raising awareness about cancer risk and in managing screening programs. One area of application is the use of AI to estimate an individual's cancer risk based on their characteristics, such as genetic factors, lifestyle, exposure to carcinogens, and medical history.AI enables the integration of data from various sources, such as individual medical records and population-based cancer registries. This can help with planning preventive, informational, and educational initiatives, as well as with designing new screening programs. Digital analysis of medical images and the identification of multidimensional relationships between various features may prove to be very useful in oncology. For example, AI significantly improved the accuracy of liver cancer risk prediction in patients with chronic hepatitis B (16). Studies haveshown that ChatGPT has significant potential for automating the delivery of information on prevention and screening to patients and that it can improve both the quality of patient education and the knowledge that patients acquire. The integration of AI into national and regional screening programs can help optimize their reach and effectiveness. In the future, further progress in this field will depend on multidisciplinary collaboration: physicians, AI researchers, public health experts, and governments must work together. With this approach, AI could help reduce the global burden of cancer. However, for many people, particularly older adults, using modern technologies remains challenging. A pilot study by Ahmed et al. (17) showed that a cancer prevention mobile app tested in six European countries could raise cancer awareness, although its usefulness was rated as moderate. Technical problems were the main reason for discontinuing use of the app.The collection of articles published in this Research Topic, "Strategies to improve awareness and management of cancer risk factors and screenings," suggests that education is essential to reducing the impact of cancer on people's lives. Identifying and reaching the appropriate age and sociodemographic groups is particularly important for reducing exposure to cancer risk factors and encouraging participation in screening programs. Technological advancements, including AI, offer new global and institutional opportunities, but individuals often prefer personal contact with a physician. Physicians remain patients' primary and preferred source of information.

title: Deep Myometrial Invasion in Superficial Spreading Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Cervix: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Background: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) can spread upward along the endometrial surface, usually without invading the uterine wall, and is difficult to separate from primary endometrial SCC involving the cervix. Case presentation: A 72-year-old woman, treated by conization for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 ten years earlier and lost to follow-up, presented with pelvic pain and a 12 × 8 cm pelvic mass. Without preoperative histology she underwent total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. A poorly differentiated non-keratinizing SCC involved the cervical mucosa with 1 mm of stromal invasion, replaced the endometrium in continuity up to the fundus and invaded 9 mm of the myometrium, more than one-half of its thickness, with focal lymphovascular space invasion. Immunohistochemistry and HPV testing were not performed. The morphology favors a cervical primary with superficial spread (FIGO 2018 stage IA1, since corpus extension is disregarded), but a primary endometrial SCC, which would be staged as endometrial cancer, cannot be excluded. No lymph nodes were examined, and PET/CT showed no residual, nodal or distant disease. The tumor board recommended pelvic radiotherapy (50.4 Gy in 28 fractions), beyond guideline recommendations for stage IA1; PET/CT six months after surgery showed no recurrence. Conclusions: The case illustrates a diagnostic problem. When an SCC replaces the endometrium and invades the myometrium while cervical invasion is minimal, its origin and stage remain uncertain without p16 and HPV testing. Detailed sampling, the explicit reporting of corpus invasion and expert pathology review should precede staging and treatment.

title: Transcriptionally active HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is associated with a coordinated meiotic gene programme and promoter hypomethylation
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus-positive (HPV+) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma exhibits distinct molecular and clinical characteristics. Although aberrant expression of germ-cell genes has been reported, it remains unclear whether this expression reflects stochastic epigenetic de-repression or a coordinated transcriptional programme. This study investigated meiotic gene activation, promoter methylation, viral transcriptional activity and cellular localisation in HPV-associated tumours. Methods Transcriptomic profiles of 279 primary tumours from The Cancer Genome Atlas were analysed using differential expression analysis and functional enrichment. A literature-curated 95-gene panel and six-gene meiotic module were evaluated across independent expression (GSE65858), methylation (GSE38266) and two single-cell sequencing cohorts (GSE181919 and GSE182227). Promoter methylation, gene co-expression, immune-cell composition and malignant-cell localisation were assessed using Mann–Whitney tests, Spearman correlations, enrichment tests, receiver operating characteristic analysis and regression models, with multiple-testing correction where applicable. Results Transcriptomic comparison of HPV + and HPV− tumours revealed distinct expression programmes involving meiosis, immune responses and epithelial differentiation. A six-gene module comprising MEI1, SMC1B, STAG3, SYCP2, SYCE2 and MAJIN showed coordinated expression and promoter hypomethylation. Module expression was inversely associated with methylation, and the methylation differences were replicated in an independent cohort. The module distinguished transcriptionally active HPV+ tumours from HPV− tumours (AUC = 0.959). In contrast, HPV DNA-positive tumours without detectable viral transcription showed no increase in module expression. Classical MAGE/CTAG cancer–testis antigens lacked comparable discrimination. Single-cell analysis and independent tumour-level validation confirmed that the meiotic signature was predominantly localised to malignant epithelial cells. HPV+ tumours also exhibited increased estimated plasma-cell and CD8-positive T-cell fractions. The association between HPV status and the meiotic signature remained significant after adjusting for anatomical site, proliferation, and tumour purity. Conclusions Transcriptionally active HPV+ head and neck carcinomas exhibit a coordinated, promoter-hypomethylated meiotic gene programme distinct from conventional cancer–testis antigen activation. These findings define a tumour-cell transcriptional signature of active HPV infection and warrant mechanistic study of how the virus alters epigenetic regulation, as well as evaluation of the signature as a biomarker.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus-positive (HPV+) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma exhibits distinct molecular and clinical characteristics. Although aberrant expression of germ-cell genes has been reported, it remains unclear whether this expression reflects stochastic epigenetic de-repression or a coordinated transcriptional programme. This study investigated meiotic gene activation, promoter methylation, viral transcriptional activity and cellular localisation in HPV-associated tumours. Methods Transcriptomic profiles of 279 primary tumours from The Cancer Genome Atlas were analysed using differential expression analysis and functional enrichment. A literature-curated 95-gene panel and six-gene meiotic module were evaluated across independent expression (GSE65858), methylation (GSE38266) and two single-cell sequencing cohorts (GSE181919 and GSE182227). Promoter methylation, gene co-expression, immune-cell composition and malignant-cell localisation were assessed using Mann–Whitney tests, Spearman correlations, enrichment tests, receiver operating characteristic analysis and regression models, with multiple-testing correction where applicable. Results Transcriptomic comparison of HPV + and HPV− tumours revealed distinct expression programmes involving meiosis, immune responses and epithelial differentiation. A six-gene module comprising MEI1, SMC1B, STAG3, SYCP2, SYCE2 and MAJIN showed coordinated expression and promoter hypomethylation. Module expression was inversely associated with methylation, and the methylation differences were replicated in an independent cohort. title: Comparative cost-effectiveness of HPV mRNA and DNA testing for anal cancer screening in MSM living with HIV: a model-based study
abstract: Anal cancer incidence is increasing among men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV, driven by persistent high-risk (HR) HPV infection. HPV mRNA testing may offer higher specificity for detecting high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) than cytology or HPV DNA testing, with potential economic implications. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of screening strategies combining HPV biomarkers and post-high-resolution anoscopy (HRA) management. A Markov model simulated a cohort of MSM living with HIV to assess 45 screening strategies varying by algorithm (cytology, co-testing, HPV reflex), HPV assay (DNA-hybridization, DNA-PCR, mRNA), and post-HRA management (follow-up, infrared coagulation [IRC], trichloroacetic acid [TCA]). Outcomes included HSIL and anal cancer cases, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), costs, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs). Strategies involving treatment reduced anal cancer incidence by 43–69% compared with no screening, with greater reductions for co-testing. Cytology was the most cost-effective option at €25 per test. At €6, co-testing became competitive, particularly with HR-HPV assays—DNA-hybridization (€13,203/QALY) and mRNA (€14,482/QALY). All optimal strategies included TCA. Anal cancer screening in MSM living with HIV is effective and cost-effective. Co-testing with cytology and HR-HPV assays—whether DNA or mRNA—combined with post-HRA treatment provided the greatest health benefits, while its cost-effectiveness depended strongly on HPV test cost and became favorable at lower HPV test costs. HPV mRNA-based approaches provided a comparable and viable alternative to HPV DNA.

title: Bruceine D induces ferroptosis in ectocervical Ect1/E6E7 cells by modulating GSTP1 and MAPK14 signaling and downregulating GPX4
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical cancer. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated malignancies. Bruceine D (BD), a bioactive quassinoid isolated from Brucea javanica, exhibits antitumor and antiviral activities. However, its effects on HPV-associated cervical epithelial cells remain unclear. METHODS: The effects of BD on HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized ectocervical epithelial cells (Ect1/E6E7) were evaluated using cell viability, colony formation, EdU incorporation, and cell-cycle assays. Ferroptosis-associated changes were assessed by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Pharmacological rescue experiments using ferroptosis inhibitors and pathway inhibitors were performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation were used to identify candidate regulatory targets. RESULTS: BD significantly inhibited Ect1/E6E7 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest in a concentration-dependent manner. BD treatment increased lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, depleted intracellular GSH, disrupted mitochondrial function, and downregulated GPX4. Ferroptosis inhibitors partially reversed BD-induced cell death, supporting the involvement of ferroptosis. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation implicated GSTP1 and MAPK14 in the cellular response to BD. Pharmacological inhibition of MAPK14 attenuated BD-induced ferroptotic responses, suggesting a role for GSTP1/MAPK14-associated signaling. BD also exhibited synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with the ferroptosis inducer erastin. CONCLUSION: BD reduces the survival of HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized cervical epithelial cells by inducing ferroptosis associated with GPX4 downregulation and GSTP1/MAPK14 signaling. These findings support further preclinical investigation of BD and ferroptosis-based approaches in HPV-associated cervical disease.

title: TNF-α genetic variants and cervical cancer risk in south India
abstract: Background : Cervical cancer, primarily caused by persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, remains a significant public health burden in India. Host genetic factors, such as polymorphisms in Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-α), may influence individual susceptibility to HPV persistence and progression to cancer. This study investigated the association of TNF-α promoter polymorphisms(-308G>A and -238G>A) and sociodemographic factors with cervical cancer risk in a South Indian population. Materials and Methods : A cross-sectional study was conducted with 80 participants (40 precancerous lesions, 40 invasive cervical cancer cases) and 80 age-matched healthy controls. HPV DNA was detected using multiplex PCR, and genotyping for the TNF-α polymorphisms was performed using Polymerase Chain Reaction-Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (PCR-RFLP). Sociodemographic data were collected via structured interviews. Associations were assessed using odds ratios(OR) with 95% confidence intervals(CI). Results : HPV DNA was detected in 97.5% of precancer and cancer cases, compared to 12.5% of controls, with HPV 16 and 18 being the predominant types. Illiteracy was significantly associated with an increased risk of invasive cancer(OR = 2.65, 95% CI: 1.055–6.655, p=0.038). However, no significant association was found between the TNF-α -308G>A(p=0.427) or -238G>A(p=0.465) polymorphisms and cervical cancer risk. The GG genotype was predominant for both SNPs in cases and controls. Conclusion : While confirming HPV as the primary etiological agent and identifying illiteracy as a key risk factor, this study found no evidence that the studied TNF-α promoter polymorphisms contribute significantly to cervical cancer susceptibility in this cohort. Public health efforts should prioritize vaccination, screening, and addressing socioeconomic determinants.

title: Scientific principles guiding risk-based cervical cancer screening in resource-limited settings
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes 660,000 cases and 350,000 deaths globally despite effective vaccination, screening, and treatment options; few are feasible to implement in resource-limited settings where the burden of cervical cancer is high. A single-dose, multivalent HPV vaccination of adolescent females could prevent the majority of cancers, making it the undisputed priority. However, vaccination programs leave a decades-long time lag between prophylaxis of HPV infection and cancer prevention in later adulthood. Screening for and treatment of precancer in mid-adulthood could save additional millions of lives. There are pertinent scientific facts concerning HPV natural history and cervical carcinogenesis so firmly established that they are beyond reasonable dispute. With the realization that scientific certainty demands extraordinary evidence that will always be further refined, a group of cervical cancer prevention specialists with experience in resource-limited settings met intending to posit such a set of fundamental scientific principles.

title: FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH UPTAKE OF THE HPV VACCINE AMONG AFRICAN AMERICAN MEN BETWEEN THE AGES OF 18 AND 26 YEARS
abstract: Study Rationale: HPV infections are prevalent, with more than 42 million Americans having contracted types of HPV that are known to cause diseases, and about 13 million Americans, including teenagers, become infected every year. This study draws from the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to examine factors associated with HPV vaccine uptake among African American men aged 18 to 26 years. Methods: A cross-sectional research design was adopted, and data were collected via an online survey administered to participants through the Rutgers Qualtrics portal. HPV vaccine uptake was assessed using self-reported measures, including receipt of at least one HPV vaccine dose (initiation), receipt of the first dose before age 18, receipt of at least one dose in the United States, and receipt of one or more doses (progression to completion). The study measures included sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of HPV, healthcare provider and peer recommendations, self-efficacy, and health-related factors. Data analysis included univariate, bivariate, and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Results: Among the 559 young African American men in the study, 89.3% had received at least one HPV vaccine, while 65.1% had received more than one HPV vaccine dose. Regarding factors associated with vaccination status, the most consistent predictors in multivariable logistic regression were younger age and recommendation by healthcare providers. Regarding vaccination initiation and progression to completion, younger age was significantly associated with increased vaccination initiation (OR = 0.77, p = .016). At the same time, recommendations by healthcare providers were positively associated with HPV vaccine initiation (OR = 2.23, p < .001) and progression to completion (OR = 2.01, p < .001). The availability of healthcare was significantly connected to more than one dose of the vaccination series (OR = 0.84, p = .049). Overall, subjective norms, especially healthcare provider recommendations, were the strongest predictors of HPV vaccine uptake. Conclusions: Recommendations from healthcare providers and the age at vaccination have the greatest influence on HPV vaccine uptake among African American men aged 18–26 years. Enhancing provider-initiated vaccination recommendations and access to vaccination could improve HPV vaccination initiation and completion in this group of individuals and, eventually, help prevent HPV-associated cancers and reduce health inequities.

title: Immune microenvironment of penile squamous cell carcinoma: HPV-driven versus HPV-independent
abstract: Penile squamous cell carcinoma (pSCC) is rare, with human papillomavirus (HPV)–driven and HPV-independent pathways that may shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). We conducted an integrative review (Whittemore and Knafl) reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Structured searches of Europe PMC and MEDLINE (13 August 2026), plus an authors’ curated bibliography, yielded 318 unique records after deduplication. Two reviewers independently screened the records; data for the 24 tabulated sources were extracted and appraised (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, MMAT v.2018) by two reviewers, and the four included studies co-authored by A.C. Synthesis was narrative; no meta-analysis was performed. In total, 121 reports (119 unique studies) were included; original research predominated ( n = 83), and HPV stratification was available in 76/121. Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1; n = 86), programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1; n = 61), and cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8; n = 47) were the most frequent TIME markers. The most reproducible HPV–TIME contrast was higher PD-L1 in HPV-independent tumors; HPV-positive tumors more often showed selected effector, myeloid, or tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) features, but unsupervised immunophenotypes were not reducible to HPV status alone. Diffuse or high tumor PD-L1, low lymphocytic infiltrate, adverse myeloid spatial patterns, and elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) recurred as adverse signals. In real-world immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) series, the objective response rate was 13% overall and 35% in lymph-node–only metastases. HPV defines a biological axis within pSCC TIME—most clearly PD-L1 enrichment in HPV-independent disease—but is not a complete immune classifier. ICI activity in advanced pSCC is clinically meaningful yet uncommon; biomarker-guided selection remains hypothesis-generating.

source_records.title: Immune microenvironment of penile squamous cell carcinoma: HPV-driven versus HPV-independent
source_records.abstract: Penile squamous cell carcinoma (pSCC) is rare, with human papillomavirus (HPV)–driven and HPV-independent pathways that may shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). We conducted an integrative review (Whittemore and Knafl) reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Structured searches of Europe PMC and MEDLINE (13 August 2026), plus an authors’ curated bibliography, yielded 318 unique records after deduplication. Two reviewers independently screened the records; data for the 24 tabulated sources were extracted and appraised (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, MMAT v.2018) by two reviewers, and the four included studies co-authored by A.C. Synthesis was narrative; no meta-analysis was performed. In total, 121 reports (119 unique studies) were included; original research predominated ( n = 83), and HPV stratification was available in 76/121. Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1; n = 86), programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1; n = 61), and cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8; n = 47) were the most frequent TIME markers. The most reproducible HPV–TIME contrast was higher PD-L1 in HPV-independent tumors; HPV-positive tumors more often showed selected effector, myeloid, or tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) features, but unsupervised immunophenotypes were not reducible to HPV status alone. Diffuse or high tumor PD-L1, low lymphocytic infiltrate, adverse myeloid spatial patterns, and elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) recurred as adverse signals. In real-world immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) series, the objective response rate was 13% overall and 35% in lymph-node–only metastases. HPV defines a biological axis within pSCC TIME—most clearly PD-L1 enrichment in HPV-independent disease—but is not a complete immune classifier. ICI activity in advanced pSCC is clinically meaningful yet uncommon; biomarker-guided selection remains hypothesis-generating.

title: Stress Biology, Vaginal Microbiome Dynamics, and Diagnostic Outcomes After Abnormal Cervical Cancer Screening: Protocol for a Digitally Enabled Multimodal Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background Cervical cancer risk is shaped by interacting psychosocial, biological, microbial, and clinical processes; however, few prospective studies integrate repeated biospecimens, ecological momentary assessment, wearable data, and electronic health record information within the same cohort. This gap is especially important in populations disproportionately affected by cervical cancer inequities. Objective This paper describes the protocol and the current implementation of a digitally enabled prospective cohort study designed to examine how psychosocial stress, cortisol regulation, vaginal microbiome dynamics, human papillomavirus–related factors, and clinical follow-up jointly influence the resolution or persistence of abnormal cervical cancer screening findings at diagnostic evaluation. Methods The study is recruiting women aged 21 to 65 years after an abnormal cervical cancer screening result and before diagnostic colposcopy. The target sample is 270 women (90 Latina, 90 non–Latina Black, and 90 non–Latina White). Study procedures include electronic health record–based prescreening; in-person consent and onboarding; baseline surveys; twice-daily ecological momentary assessment for 14 days; home salivary cortisol collection; passive Fitbit monitoring; retrieval of residual Pap (Papanicolaou) material from the index abnormal screen (T0); blood, urine, saliva, vaginal pH, and a self-collected vaginal swab at baseline (T1); and provider-collected vaginal and cervical sampling at follow-up colposcopy (T2). Data are integrated across Epic, REDCap, participant-facing digital tools, biospecimen workflows, and pathology-linked outcomes. The 2 coprimary confirmatory analyses use Firth bias-reduced logistic regression to estimate the adjusted odds of persistence associated with a standardized baseline 10-item Perceived Stress Scale score and a standardized participant-level mean diurnal cortisol slope, controlling for age, race or ethnicity, and index screening risk stratum. Results Recruitment began in September 2025. As of July 15, 2026, 180 women had been prescreened, 25 had met eligibility criteria, 24 had been contacted, 13 had completed direct screening, 8 had declined participation, 3 participants had enrolled, and 2 had completed the study. Recruitment and longitudinal data collection are expected to continue through December 2028, after which primary analyses will evaluate multilevel associations among stress, cortisol, vaginal microbiome features, human papillomavirus–related factors, and the resolution or persistence of screening outcomes at diagnostic follow-up. Conclusions This prospective cohort study provides a protocol model for equity-focused, prospective cohort research to examine multilevel drivers of women’s health. By integrating psychosocial, biological, digital, and clinical data across multiple time points, the study is positioned to inform both mechanistic research on pathways underlying the resolution or persistence of abnormal cervical cancer screening results and implementation strategies for complex, participant-centered longitudinal studies.

title: Incidence of cervical cancer in hrHPV-positive patients with low-grade cytological abnormalities: a Dutch nationwide cohort study
abstract: Background The Dutch cervical cancer screening program uses primary high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing, with cytology triage, and referral for colposcopy for all hrHPV-positive women with cytological abnormalities. However, most low-grade abnormalities regress spontaneously, raising concerns regarding overtreatment and unnecessary pressure on the healthcare system. This study aimed to assess the incidence of cervical cancer among hrHPV-positive women with low-grade cytological abnormalities compared with repeated negative for intraepithelial lesion of malignancy (NILM) cytology results, to explore whether these findings support further evaluation of risk-based follow-up strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study including women who participated in the Dutch population-based cervical cancer screening program between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2018. The inclusion period was chosen to align with the initial implementation phase of the revised Dutch screening program, which transitioned in 2017 from cytology-based to primary hrHPV testing. Eligible women were hrHPV-positive with low-grade triage cytology at baseline and hrHPV-positive women with NILM cytology at triage and one-year follow-up. The primary outcome was the five-year cumulative incidence of cervical cancer. This follow-up period corresponds to the interval used in the Dutch national cervical cancer screening program, incorporating the subsequent routine screening round after the baseline hrHPV-positive test. Adjusted analyses were not performed since relevant potential confounders were not available in the nationwide screening registry. This study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, ID NCT07259616. Findings The five-year cumulative incidence of cervical cancer of 22,891 hrHPV-positive women with low-grade triage cytology was 0.47% (107/22,891; 95% CI 0.39–0.56). Among these women, 18,898 had ≤ cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) I at baseline colposcopy, their five-year cumulative incidence was 0.25% (47/18,898; 95% CI 0.19–0.33). Women with ≤ CIN I and persistent low-grade cytology at one-year follow-up had a five-year cumulative incidence of 0.13% (16/12,592; 95% CI 0.08–0.20). The five-year cumulative incidence among 23,188 hrHPV-positive women with NILM cytology at triage and one-year follow-up was 0.25% (58/23,188; 95% CI 0.19–0.32). Interpretation HrHPV-positive women with low-grade triage cytology, ≤ CIN I at baseline, and persistent low-grade cytology at one-year follow-up have a low five-year cumulative incidence of cervical cancer, which was numerically similar to that observed among women with persistent NILM cytology within the Dutch screening program. Differences in clinical management between groups may have introduced verification bias, as women with low-grade cytology underwent immediate colposcopic assessment whereas women with persistent NILM cytology did not. Given potential verification bias and residual confounding, these hypothesis-generating findings should be interpreted cautiously and warrant confirmation in studies with longer follow-up and prospective risk stratification. Funding No funding was received.

title: Burden and temporal trends of cervical cancer in reproductive-age females from 1990 to 2021 and projections to 2035 in G20 countries: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer remains a critical global health threat. Despite its member states accounting for more than 85% of global gross domestic product (GDP), no comprehensive assessment of cervical cancer burden exists across the diverse Group of Twenty (G20) economies. This study aimed to characterize long-term cervical cancer burden trends and project future epidemiological trajectories among G20 reproductive-age females. METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, we analyzed cervical cancer disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) among females aged 15-49 years in G20 countries (1990-2021) via Joinpoint regression, health inequality indices, Das Gupta decomposition, and Bayesian age-period-cohort projection to 2035. RESULTS: In 2021, cervical cancer generated 2.27 million DALYs among G20 reproductive-age females, with age-standardized rates ranging from 24.89 (Saudi Arabia) to 667.65 (South Africa) per 100,000. Overall rates declined (annual average percent change [AAPC]=-1.40%) (1990-2021), with China achieving a notable reduction (AAPC=-1.51%), but increased in Russia (AAPC=1.70%), Japan (AAPC=0.65%), Italy (AAPC=0.33%), and South Africa (AAPC=0.14%). Sociodemographic Index (SDI)-related inequality narrowed (1990: Slope Index of Inequality [SII]=-349.58, Concentration Index=-0.21; 2021: SII=-261.82, Concentration Index=-0.18), but persisted. Population growth (+23.99%) and age structure changes (+20.92%) drove DALY increases in the G20, offset by epidemiological improvements (-43.92%). Most G20 countries will see declining burden by 2035, while South Africa faces the largest increase. CONCLUSION: Differentiated, evidence-based strategies tailored to national burden characteristics, addressing demographic shifts, key health system gaps, and human papillomavirus genotype disparities, are critically needed to successfully achieve the World Health Organization 2030 global cervical cancer elimination targets.

title: ПОВРЕЖДЕНИЕ КАМБИАЛЬНЫХ КЛЕТОК У ПАЦИЕНТОВ С СУПЕРИНФЕКЦИЕЙ SARS-CОV-2 И ВПЧ. ОТДАЛЕННЫЕ ФИБРОПРОЛИФЕРАТИВНЫЕ ПОСЛЕДСТВИЯ
abstract: В настоящей работе проведено исследование по изучению реакции камбиальных (стволовых) клеток при инфицировании вирусом папилломы человека (ВПЧ) и вирусом SARS-CoV-2 [1, 2, 3]. Проведён анализ литературы, подтверждающий связь между персистенцией вирусов, дисрегуляцией стволовых клеток и развитием фиброза This acticle presents a comparative analysis of two independent studies devoted to examining the response of stem (cambial) cells to infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV) and the SARS‐CoV‐2 virus [1, 2, 3]. An analysis of the literature has been carried out, confirming the link between viral persistence, dysregulation of stem cells, and the development of fibrosis

Проведён анализ литературы, подтверждающий связь между персистенцией вирусов, дисрегуляцией стволовых клеток и развитием фиброза This acticle presents a comparative analysis of two independent studies devoted to examining the response of stem (cambial) cells to infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV) and the SARS‐CoV‐2 virus [1, 2, 3]. An analysis of the literature has been carried out, confirming the link between viral persistence, dysregulation of stem cells, and the development of fibrosis

title: Longitudinal profiling of soluble immune checkpoint proteins in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: treatment-associated dynamics and exploratory associations with disease stage and relapse-free survival
abstract: Introduction Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is now predominantly associated with human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV16, and is characterized by a distinct immune landscape and a generally favorable prognosis. Nonetheless, a subset of patients relapses following curative treatment, emphasizing the need for biomarkers that capture dynamic systemic immune regulation beyond tissue-based analyses. Soluble immune checkpoint proteins (sICPs) are biologically active circulating mediators that may reflect the balance between anti-tumor immunity and immune tolerance. Methods In this prospective observational study, we longitudinally profiled serum levels of 17 sICPs in 77 patients with OPSCC who received curative-intent radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy. Serum samples were collected at three time points: pre-treatment (baseline), 7 weeks after treatment initiation, and at 12 months after treatment completion, and analyzed in relation to sampling time point, tumor stage, treatment modality, and clinical outcome. Results Among 65 HPV16 + /p16 + patients, distinct treatment-associated temporal changes were observed, including a transient increase in soluble TIM-3 and a concomitant decrease in soluble PD-1 during active therapy, followed by partial recovery at long-term follow-up. At 12 months after treatment completion, soluble CD40 levels were elevated, while soluble TLR-2 levels were reduced, indicating persistent remodeling of systemic immune regulation beyond active treatment. Tumor stages II-IVA were associated with increased baseline levels of inhibitory sICPs, including soluble GITRL and soluble CTLA-4, compared with stage I, and a trend toward reduced soluble CD80 levels, suggesting a more immunosuppressive systemic milieu in advanced disease. Importantly, elevated pre-treatment soluble PD-1 was associated with poorer relapse-free survival in the entire cohort of 77 patients, although this association was not observed in the HPV16 + /p16 + subgroup alone. No other sICP retained prognostic significance after correction for multiple testing. Discussion Given the sample size and limited number of events, the association between baseline sPD-1 and RFS in the entire cohort should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Together, these findings indicate that circulating sICPs undergo dynamic and sustained changes during and after treatment and support further investigation of their associations with systemic immune status and clinical outcomes in larger, prospectively powered OPSCC cohorts.

title: A six-gene DNA methylation panel in cervical scrapes for cross-sectional discrimination of cervical lesions and cancer
abstract: Background Accurate assessment of cervical lesion severity is crucial for precise diagnosis and timely clinical decision-making. DNA methylation, which can be readily detected using molecular methods, has emerged as a promising approach for identifying biomarkers for cervical cancer screening and triage. However, previous studies primarily reported binary positive/negative rates without characterizing the continuous quantitative spectrum of ΔCp changes across lesion grades. This study aimed to evaluate the ΔCp values of six markers (ASTN1, DLX1, ITGA4, RXFP3, SOX17, and ZNF671) for cross-sectional discrimination of cervical lesion severity. Methods We used quantitative methylation-specific polymerase chain reaction (qMSP) to measure the methylation levels of the six markers in cervical scrapes. The results were expressed as ΔCp values (Cp target – Cp reference), with ACHE serving as the reference gene for normalization. The study cohort comprised 14 cases of cervical cancer (CC), 23 cases of CIN3, 53 cases of CIN2, 115 cases of CIN1, and 55 normal cases. All patients underwent HPV testing, ThinPrep cytological testing (TCT), colposcopic biopsy, and DNA methylation analysis. ΔCp values of ASTN1, DLX1, ITGA4, RXFP3, SOX17, and ZNF671 generally decreased across histological grades from normal tissue to CIN1, CIN2, CIN3, and cervical cancer. Results These markers exhibited superior performance in detecting CIN2+ and in cross-sectional discrimination of invasive cancer within the CIN2+ subgroup. For differentiating CIN1- from CIN2+, AUCs for the six individual methylation markers ranged from 0.707 to 0.816 using 1,000 bootstrap resamples for 95% confidence intervals. These values were higher than those observed for TCT (AUC = 0.554), Other HPV only (AUC = 0.354), and HPV16/18 testing (AUC = 0.653). Among the six markers, ZNF671 demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for detecting CIN2+ (AUC = 0.816, 95% CI: 0.763-0.867). In the CIN2+ subgroup, marker AUCs for distinguishing invasive cancer from CIN2/3 ranged from 0.804 to 0.854. Conclusions Quantitative DNA methylation profiling of the predefined six-gene panel provides information for cross-sectional discrimination of cervical lesion severity in cervical scrape samples, with ZNF671 showing the strongest single-marker performance in this cohort.

title: Integrating spatial and single-cell multi-omics analysis of induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cervical adenocarcinoma model
abstract: Human papillomavirus 18 (HPV18) preferentially infects cervical stem cell-like cells and is strongly associated with adenocarcinoma. However, the mechanisms underlying differentiation into cervical adenocarcinoma remain unclear due to the lack of appropriate experimental models. We aimed to establish an iRC-based model and characterize molecular and cellular features associated with adenocarcinoma-like differentiation in the context of HPV18 E6/E7 expression. HPV18 E6/E7 were introduced into induced reserve cell-like cells (iRCs) to generate tumor models. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell multi-omics analyses integrated histological and molecular data. A distinct component (Gland_A) exhibited morphological and immunohistochemical features of cervical adenocarcinoma and was efficiently induced in iRC-18 tumors. Gland_A showed increased chromatin accessibility and elevated expression of FOXA1, FOXA2, and ALDH1A1. Clinical samples confirmed enrichment of ALDH1A1 in HPV-associated adenocarcinomas. This model recapitulates key adenocarcinoma-like features associated with HPV18 E6/E7 expression and provides a complementary experimental system for investigating cervical adenocarcinoma differentiation.
